courses.name: American Sign Language and Deaf Culture 10, 20, 30
courses.subject: Languages

outcomes.statement: Select, use and reflect on basic strategies to interpret American Sign Language messages.
outcomes.printedWith: * For further information and suggestions for additional strategies, see Appendix A.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Use and reflect on basic metacognitive strategies*, with guidance, to enhance language learning, such as:
- construct a plan for new learning tasks with the guidance of the teacher;
- reflect on the communication process by checking copied signing for accuracy; or,
- keep a learning log to gain awareness of which language learning strategies are most effective.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and reflect on basic interactive and affective strategies*, with guidance, to enhance language learning, such as:
- seek the assistance of a friend to interpret text;
- repeat what someone has signed to confirm mutual understanding; or,
- recognize common facial expressions as part of ASL communication.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and reflect on basic interpretive strategies*, with guidance, to enhance language learning, such as:
- replay familiar self-chosen recorded video texts to enhance understanding and enjoyment;
- use gestures, illustrations and contextual clues to aid comprehension of unfamiliar signs; or,
- endeavour to read finger-spelled words as whole units rather than letter by letter.

outcomes.statement: Select, use and reflect on basic strategies to begin expressing oneself in American Sign Language.
outcomes.printedWith: * For further information and suggestions for additional strategies, see Appendix A.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Use and reflect on basic cognitive strategies*, with guidance, to enhance communication, such as:
- identify similarities and differences between aspects of ASL and students’ other languages;
- imitate signed words and sentences; or,
- memorize new sign vocabulary by repeating it or signing/finger-spelling it.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and reflect on basic interactive and affective strategies*, with guidance, to enhance communication, such as:
- recognize and respond to turn-taking cues;
- check with peers or teacher regarding accuracy of sign choice and production; or,
- experiment with basic forms of expression in simple conversations and note their acceptance or non-acceptance by more experienced signers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and reflect on basic productive strategies*, with guidance, to enhance communication, such as:
- increase signing vocabulary by copying what others sign, practising signs that are visible in the immediate environment and using resources;
- supplement signed communications with a variety of non-verbal cues (e.g., mime, pointing, gesturing, drawing pictures, illustrations, dramatization); or,
- apply knowledge of iconic signs that look like their intended meaning (e.g., eat, drink, sit) to communicate meaning by experimenting with other similar iconic signs.

outcomes.statement: Construct, with support, the meaning of simple signed texts in American Sign Language.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize and understand the complete manual alphabet, basic ASL hand shapes and numbers 1 – 20.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Comprehend a repertoire of high frequency words and phrases used to communicate in predictable contexts such as when with friends and family or during holidays.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze the relationships between common handshapes and location of signs, common facial expressions and their role in making different meanings.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify basic ASL structures such as questions and statements.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: View and understand, in guided situations, a variety of visuals and other media and communication forms (e.g., charts, graphics, illustrations, videos, digital media) to aid in signing comprehension.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine the cultural influences on signed language including Plains Indian Sign Language, Langue des Signes Québécoise (LSQ) and Black American Sign Language.

outcomes.statement: Produce, with support, simple signed texts that demonstrate basic understanding of American Sign Language.
outcomes.printedWith: *For further information and suggestions for additional grammatical elements, see Appendix B.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate basic conversational conventions (e.g., greeting, nodding in acknowledgment).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Produce complete manual alphabet, basic ASL hand shapes and the numbers 1 – 20.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Combine high frequency words and phrases to communicate with basic signed sentences in predictable contexts such as greetings, sharing basic personal information or activities in the home.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Indicate intent of communication clearly using basic ASL structures such as questions and statements.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Express meaning, in guided situations, using a variety of visuals and other media and communication forms.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Practise, with the assistance of a model of specific linguistic elements, grammatical elements* such as gender signs, yes/no questions or cardinal and ordinal numbers.

outcomes.statement: Apply knowledge of American Sign Language, in predictable situations and for basic purposes, to receive information, extend knowledge of the world, achieve objectives and for enjoyment.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Summarize the main idea from simple signed texts on predictable topics such as local community or activities in the home.

indicators.label: b

outcomes.statement: Select, use and reflect on a variety of strategies to interpret American Sign Language messages.
outcomes.printedWith: * For further information and suggestions for additional strategies, see Appendix A.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Use and reflect on a variety of metacognitive strategies* to enhance language learning, such as:
- make a plan in advance about how to approach a language learning task;
- reflect on the communication process, including attending and signing, by checking copied signing for accuracy and monitoring own sign production to check for persistent errors; or,
- keep a learning log to evaluate own performance and identify which language learning strategies are most effective.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and reflect on a variety of interactive and affective strategies* to enhance language learning, such as:
- work with a friend to identify patterns and relationships in signs;
- summarize the point reached in a discussion to help focus the talk and ask follow-up questions to check for understanding; or,
- recognize facial expressions as an essential component of ASL.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and reflect on a variety of interpretive strategies* to enhance language learning, such as:
- view a variety of video recordings to ensure exposure to regional, cultural and gender signing variations;
- use knowledge of the context to aid comprehension and ask for things to be repeated in order to understand complex ideas; or,
- mentally prepare questions and make predictions about new information based on prior knowledge and personal experience.

outcomes.statement: Select, use and reflect on a variety of strategies to express oneself in American Sign Language.
outcomes.printedWith: * For further information and suggestions for additional strategies, see Appendix A.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Use and reflect on a variety of cognitive strategies* to enhance communication, such as:
- compare and contrast aspects of ASL and students’ other languages;
- group together sets of signs (vocabulary, structures) with similar characteristics; or,
- make information easier to understand and remember by using reference points and initiatives like classifiers and body shifts.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and reflect on a variety of interactive and affective strategies* to enhance communication, such as:
- work cooperatively with peers in small groups to rehearse or role-play language use;
- assess feedback from conversation partner to recognize when the message has not been understood (e.g., squinted eyes, blank look, head shake) and start again using a different tactic when communication breaks down; or,
- use new signs which occur in conversations, making use of them as soon as appropriate and asking for confirmation that a form used is appropriate.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and reflect on a variety of productive strategies* to enhance communication, such as:
- apply knowledge of sentence patterns and ASL structure to form new sentences;
- employ circumlocution and definition to compensate for gaps in vocabulary; or
- practise facial expressions, movement, location and non-manual signals (e.g., facial expressions, mouth morphemes, head nod/shake, shoulder shift/contrastive structure/spatial organization) to assist in effective communication.

outcomes.statement: ST30.1 Select, use and assess a variety of strategies to interpret American Sign Language messages.
outcomes.printedWith: * For further information and suggestions for additional strategies, see Appendix A.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Use and assess a variety of metacognitive strategies* to enhance language learning, such as:
- independently execute a plan to engage in a new language learning task;
- assess communication process by being aware of own strengths and weaknesses, identify needs and goals and organize strategies and procedures accordingly; or,
- keep a learning log to evaluate their own performance or comprehension at the end of a task and assess which language learning strategies are most effective.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and assess a variety of interactive and affective strategies* to enhance language learning, such as:
- collaborate with others to identify how patterns and relationships in signs assist in interpreting meaning;
- summarize the point reached in a discussion to help focus the talk and ask follow-up questions to check for understanding; or,
- recognize nuances in facial expressions as essential components of communicating in ASL.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and assess a variety of interpretive strategies* to enhance language learning, such as:
- view a variety of video recordings to compare and contrast regional, cultural and gender signing variations;
- assess own information needs and prepare questions or a guide to note information found in a signed text; or,
- perceive and note down unknown signs and sign-expressions, noting also their context and function.

outcomes.statement: Select, use and assess a variety of strategies to express oneself in American Sign Language.
outcomes.printedWith: * For further information and suggestions for additional strategies, see Appendix A.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Use and assess a variety of cognitive strategies* to enhance communication, such as:
- assess similarities and differences between aspects of ASL and students’ other languages;
- group together sets of signs (e.g., vocabulary, structures) with similar characteristics and use induction to generate rules governing language use; or,
- make information easier to understand and remember by using reference points and initiatives like classifiers and body shifts.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and assess a variety of interactive and affective strategies* to enhance communication, such as:
- participate cooperatively in conferencing, brainstorming and debating and invite others into the discussion;
- initiate or maintain interaction with signers who are deaf, deafened or hard of hearing; or,
- use a range of fillers, hesitation devices and gambits to sustain conversations.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Practise and assess a variety of productive strategies* to enhance communication, such as:
- employ rhythm and symmetry in signs and use familiar patterns appropriate for various genres;
- revise and improve expressive communications by using knowledge of patterns and structures in ASL to form new sentences; or,
- rephrase difficult structures or strategically use circumlocution to clarify communication.

outcomes.statement: Research artists who create work in response to the natural world.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Generate questions for inquiry regarding artists who are inspired by nature. For example:
- How do artists use materials from nature?
- How do First Nations and Métis artists express cultural and historical connections to the land?
- How did nature inspire a selected artwork (e.g., comments on sustainability, seasonal imagery in Japanese art)?

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Research artists who are inspired by the natural world such as:
- eco-friendly artists, soundscapes composers, place-based performance artists; or,
- First Nations drummers, singers, dancers and regalia designers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Document the research process (e.g., digital documentation, research notes, journal entries).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Share research findings with peers and/or others (e.g., in person, virtual presentations).

outcomes.statement: Apply creative processes for producing arts expressions within a local context.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss and examine how creating in the arts is a process that can be explored in multiple ways (e.g., imagining, planning, researching, generating, experimenting, risking, observing, drafting, reflecting, documenting, practicing, refining, sharing).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss how place-based inquiry is dependent on the local context (e.g., locale, people, history, season).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research local place (e.g., local artists, history, geography) as inspiration for arts expression.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine and conduct a place-based artistic inquiry, drawing on ideas, resources and influences from one’s place (e.g., current urban issues, rural or land-based sources of inspiration, newcomers’ worldviews, First Nations and Métis perspectives on local historic events, environmental or social sustainability concerns).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Utilize technology as a tool to organize, express and share ideas.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Create place-based arts expressions (e.g., compose music inspired by community, use found objects in visual art, create dance in response to community issue, create drama about local history).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Document and reflect on the creative process (e.g., challenges, discoveries).

outcomes.statement: Design and produce, individually or collaboratively, a multidisciplinary arts expression.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research multidisciplinary arts examples to use as inspiration for own work (e.g., interview artists in person or online, search for project examples).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Experiment with various tools, materials, techniques and technologies to combine multiple arts disciplines.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Create a multidisciplinary project (e.g., individual student or small groups combine art forms, some students combine arts with other disciplines such as science or math).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Document and reflect on ideas, skills, techniques and technologies incorporated in own multidisciplinary project (e.g., individual project or collaborative work).

outcomes.statement: Communicate ideas that have personal meaning, creatively through the arts.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Reflect on personal experiences as possible sources of inspiration for arts expression.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Experiment with various techniques and skills to express personal meaning (e.g., memory, event, experience, concern, interest).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Communicate, through the arts, thoughts and feelings about an idea, event or concept that has personal meaning.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Take risks and discuss the value of mistakes and challenges in contributing to growth.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Collaborate to construct criteria to use when providing feedback throughout the creative process.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Apply feedback to improve creative work.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the communication of ideas and intent of own work.

outcomes.statement: Investigate use of own and others’ artistic voice.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Investigate inquiry questions such as:
- How is voice represented in each art form?
- How does one develop artistic voice?
- How do we see voice expressed in the work of others?

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Reflect on own ideas and development of artistic voice (e.g., identifying one’s preferred style, experimenting with ideas of personal relevance, expressing one’s sense of humour).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Express ideas in own style and personal voice.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss potential meanings of ‘artistic merit’.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Establish goals and work towards developing a sense of ‘artistic merit’ in an area of the arts and discover possible engagements within the community.

outcomes.statement: Collaborate with peers and others to build an arts community with a shared purpose.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Decide on a shared purpose for an arts expression/project.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Develop through collaboration with peers and others, where applicable, a plan for the creation of artistic work.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Create an artistic work with a shared purpose.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Gather feedback on the artistic work during the process and at project completion.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Construct rubrics with peers to determine expectations for collaborative work.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Reflect on strengths of the work and challenges overcome.

outcomes.statement: Conduct an inquiry into how the arts can challenge or reinforce societal norms of a given time and place.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Generate questions for inquiry into how the arts reinforce or challenge norms of various time periods.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research and discuss examples of controversial arts expressions.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the influence of pop culture on societal norms.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine selected First Nations, Métis and international Indigenous artists who challenge societal inequities through their arts (e.g., treaty education outcome SI11 - analyze how the unfulfilled aspects of treaties, with international Indigenous people, have resulted in inequities).

outcomes.statement: Investigate artistic pathways and potential careers within the arts, or other creative fields, of personal interest.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Begin to develop a portfolio of examples that demonstrate skills and interests in the arts.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore a creative opportunity one might pursue.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate and identify creative careers that would suit one’s strengths, beliefs and interests.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine working conditions associated with careers in the arts (e.g., travel requirements, working project to project, earning potential, training and professional development opportunities and costs, intense periods of work followed by gaps in employment, maintaining or sharing an artistic space, opportunities for scholarships and grants).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the role of promotion and advocacy if pursuing a career in the arts (e.g., advertising online, social media).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Refine personal learning plan for continued development and involvement in the arts (e.g., find people in community that share one’s interests).

outcomes.statement: Investigate how the arts support, influence and shape diverse communities (e.g., gender and sexual diversity, people with disabilities, ethnic groups, popular music sub-cultures, social media-based groups).

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine local arts expressions and discuss the benefits to communities.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Generate inquiry questions concerning the value of the arts for all members of communities.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Advocate for the arts in own communities (e.g., create an visual display, exhibition or performance, commercial advertisement, podcast).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Participate in a service learning opportunity involving the arts (e.g., performance at seniors’ home, raising money for foodbank through drama or dance production, selling art work).

outcomes.statement: Explore connections between the arts and ways of knowing (e.g., multicultural, Indigenous, multiple literacies, emotional, intuitive, STEAM disciplines).

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Generate inquiry questions to examine the meaning of “ways of knowing” such as:
- What are some cultural ways of knowing?
- What are some subject area or discipline-based ways of knowing?
- What is meant by multiple literacies?

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research artists to discover how the work was/is created and its sources of inspiration (e.g., Leonardo’s images, Jane Ash Poitras’ images, Martha Graham’s technique, A Tribe Called Red’s electronic music).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research and engage (e.g., in person, online) with artists from various cultural backgrounds to explore connections between the arts and diverse worldviews.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the work of artists who incorporate diverse disciplines within their arts practice (e.g., STEAM - science, technology, engineering, arts, mathematics) and incorporate interdisciplinary ideas into own work.

outcomes.statement: Examine how artists use arts to raise awareness about place and sustainability (e.g., social, economic, environmental).

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into ways that artists respond to the natural world without harming the environment (e.g., How do artists source and harvest resources sustainably?).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine arts expressions created in response to diverse environments (e.g., constructed, imagined, ecological).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research Indigenous artists whose work incorporates cultural references and/or reflects concern for sustainability.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the use of arts as activism in various places (e.g., locally, nationally, internationally).

outcomes.statement: Create original work in selected arts disciplines, individually and/or collaboratively.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate inspiration and departure points for own artistic work.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Engage in creative processes to develop artistic projects individually or collaboratively (e.g., choreographic process, visual art-making process, music composition process, dramatic/theatrical process).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Document the creative process and discuss one’s ideas, decisions and problem-solving.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Take risks and recognize the value of mistakes.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore and incorporate use of digital technologies in arts expressions.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Reflect on experiences of self, peers and others as potential inspiration for creative work.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Create personal goals, timelines and assessments for selected artistic project.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss critically one’s ideas and progress towards goals of selected artistic project.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Document development of skills and techniques in selected artistic project.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Demonstrate increased autonomy and innovation in arts expressions.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Share work and discuss ideas, artistic intent and process of creating with peers and/or audiences (e.g., written artist statements, after performance reviews or talks).

outcomes.statement: Produce and present to an audience, an individually or collaboratively created multidisciplinary arts expression.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine contemporary practices in multidisciplinary arts expressions.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Design and present, individually or collectively, a multidisciplinary work for an audience.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assume responsibility for the role of multidisciplinary artist and/or production crew member (e.g., sound designer, scenic designer, choreographer, dancer, visual effects technician, dramatic artist, makeup designer).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Apply technologies in multidisciplinary art works and/or productions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Work with others (e.g., peers, cultural groups, guest artists) on multidisciplinary art works, presentations or productions.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss evolving fields of practice that integrate or combine arts disciplines (e.g., interdisciplinary artistic practices).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Create own work inspired by contemporary multidisciplinary work of others.

outcomes.statement: Communicate ideas of social relevance, creatively through the arts.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Represent ideas, communicate messages, thoughts and feelings through arts expressions.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate artistic styles to use as inspiration for own work.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate growth of techniques and skills in one or more arts disciplines.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Develop and share artistic creations using ideas based on a topic of social relevance to students.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Create presentations of own work.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Reflect on how one’s arts expression connects with an audience.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Represent and/or challenge society through own arts expressions.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Share work live or using digital technologies.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Take risks and discuss the value of mistakes and challenges in contributing to growth.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Create goals and criteria for self improvement.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Collaborate with peers to construct criteria to use when providing feedback throughout the creative process.

outcomes.statement: Apply artistic voice with purpose.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply skills and strategies to express own voice through the arts.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Reflect on own ideas and development of artistic voice.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Set goals for growth and development of personal expression.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Express point of view through selected arts discipline.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Respond to the perspectives and artistic voices of others.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Refine own work to develop voice.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Document own work (e.g., process portfolios, evidence, digital).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the role of the arts in developing self understanding.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify personal style leading to personal voice.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect on the value of art and share perspectives with others.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Research career opportunities within the community and beyond to continue the artistic journey.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Discuss ways to continue engaging with the arts (e.g., professional, community member).

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate leadership in an arts community through shared purpose.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the meaning and importance of ‘arts community’ (e.g., What are some of the arts communities that exist locally or globally? What can be learned from them?).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research local arts communities (e.g., collectives, arts advocacy groups, funding organizations).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Build and share understanding of the value of building communities through the arts.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create a community, in own classroom, through a shared focus.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the purpose of arts organizations in supporting communities of artists (e.g., CARFAC, Listen to Dis’, OSAC, SK Arts, SaskCulture).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine the social, economic and personal benefits of belonging to arts communities.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss ways to engage and sustain communities through the arts (e.g., How can we honour existing connections? How can we bring families into the school and share learning with others?).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Design, plan and carry out a student-created arts collective (e.g., storyteller collective, visual art collective).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text:
Generate inquiry questions to explore big ideas such as:
- engagement (e.g., how to involve families, outreach).
- connecting and sharing and teaching talents within the students’ own world.

outcomes.statement: Create an arts expression to challenge, reinforce or draw attention to ideas or societal norms.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Generate ideas for investigation and examine how various artists have responded to those ideas.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss how arts expressions evolve and influence societal norms (e.g., artists as agents of social change).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research Indigenous artists whose work challenged or challenges the norms of a particular time and place (e.g., treaty education outcome HC12 - examine how treaties within contemporary society impact on individual’s lives).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Propose and create an arts expression to draw attention to a concern or idea of personal interest.

outcomes.statement: Examine how learning gained through the arts may be transferrable to careers and personal pathways.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Reflect on and discuss transferable skills (e.g., communication, digital skills, collaborative processes, creative problem solving, self expression, empathy, innovation, being able to construct).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compile and share a creative portfolio (e.g., an organized collection of work showcasing one’s creativity, abilities and thinking skills).

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Discuss the benefits of networking including how to find collaborators and support other artists and arts communities.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect on own life goals and assess how one’s creative skills could be applied in various fields.

outcomes.statement: Examine and express how the arts provide opportunities to learn about oneself.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Reflect on own art works and personal growth.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Construct assessment criteria and set goals for own work.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Document own progress.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Invite feedback from peers (e.g., dialogue, personal responses).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Plan ways to share own work and make connections with community (e.g., class, school, external groups).

outcomes.statement: Investigate how the arts engage people holistically, including physically, spiritually, intellectually and emotionally.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the holistic nature of the arts and the benefits to wellbeing and mental health (e.g., connect with teachers, community leaders, artists, Elders, online experts, counsellors).

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Investigate how artists reveal connections of body, mind and spirit through their practices.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss examples of First Nations and Métis arts expressions that engage people physically, spiritually, intellectually and emotionally (e.g., treaty education outcome SI12 - investigate the values and beliefs of self, family, community, and society in relation to the importance of honouring the spirit and intent of treaties).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect on connections between own arts expressions and the spiritual, physical, emotional and intellectual domains (e.g., How does my work connect to one or more domains?).

outcomes.statement: Investigate contemporary arts practices as a response to place and time.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Generate inquiry questions to help develop understanding of what contemporary practice means (e.g., What is contemporary arts practice?).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Examine the work of artists who respond to contemporary social issues as potential points of inspiration such as:
- How are artists responding to current social justice issues (e.g., marginalization of newcomers, bias or hatred based on race or gender and sexual diversity, economic inequities, environmental and social sustainability)?
- How do First Nations and Métis arts expressions reflect historical and contemporary concerns (e.g., treaty education outcome TPP12 indicator - examine the importance of decolonization as a process that supports the understanding that We Are All Treaty People.)?

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Respond to site-specific arts expressions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate immersive and interactive arts (e.g., moving from place to place, non-traditional performance and exhibition spaces, virtual spaces).

outcomes.statement: Apply injury prevention principles to ensure safe work performance in the autobody trade.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1A: Injury Prevention (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify industry standard personal protective equipment (PPE), including dust masks, approved respirators, coveralls, chemical resistant gloves, eye and hearing protection and footwear.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify, label, store and handle hazardous materials according to Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS 2015).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess the fire plan for the work area, including components such as fire alarms, fire extinguishers, exits and procedures, and make recommendations for improvements.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Assess hazards and apply appropriate safety procedures when working in a confined space.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Disconnect batteries and other power sources prior to undertaking autobody repairs where appropriate.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe ways to reduce personal injury or material and equipment damage as a result of unsafe work acts or environments.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the proper procedures to follow to report a workplace injury.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Apply safe and fair work practices, including freedom from violence, harassment and bullying.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Assess the ergonomic design of the work space and implement appropriate procedures to ensure safety.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Implement a plan for a safe and healthy classroom and shop environment.

outcomes.statement: Examine the evolution and characteristics of automobile design.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2: Automobile Design (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the history of automobile design from various eras and places and discuss characteristics of selected models.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify major (e.g., roof, floor, quarter panels, cowl section and rocker panels) and minor (e.g., front fenders, hood, trunk lid, door and splash pans) exterior automobile body components.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare body-on-frame, unibody and modified unitized automobile body construction.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how different types of glass (e.g., laminated and tempered) are designed to prevent injuries to automobile occupants.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research required qualities and skills necessary to design automobiles.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine how financial considerations can impact automobile design.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the effect of relevant federal legislation and regulations (e.g., safety) on automobile design.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Create, using drawing skills, computer-aided design programs or model-making, an innovative automobile body considering factors such as safety, fuel efficiency, occupant comfort and ride, ergonomics, automobile use and styling.

outcomes.statement: Use and maintain autobody hand tools and equipment following safe procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3: Hand Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe how to use hand tools such as wrenches, screwdrivers, pliers, body hammers, chisels, dolly blocks, files, pulling tools, picking tools and hand cutting tools safely.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Perform correct procedures for a specific autobody repair using appropriate hand tools.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Inspect hand tools before use and tag for repair as required.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Maintain and store hand tools and equipment appropriately.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research the cost of purchasing hand tools to enter the autobody trade.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent work-related injuries from the improper use of hand tools.

outcomes.statement: Use and maintain autobody power tools and equipment following safe procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Power Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe how power tools such as grinders, drills, drill presses, nibblers, die grinders, cut-off wheels, files, featheredgers, ratchets and impact wrenches safely.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Perform correct procedures for a specific autobody repair using appropriate power tools.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Inspect power tools before use and tag for repair as required.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Maintain and store power tools and equipment appropriately.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research the cost of purchasing power tools to enter the autobody trade.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent work-related injuries from the improper use of power tools.

outcomes.statement: Use gas metal art welding (GMAW) equipment to complete specified autobody welds.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5A: Welding in Autobody (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-12 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate knowledge of GMAW equipment such as nozzles, contact tips, liners, wire rolls, gauges and flow meters, amperage adjustment and voltage adjustment.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the importance of employing correct start-up and shut-down procedures for GMAW equipment including checking and cleaning up the work station.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare various types of wire and shielding gases used for GMAW.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Disassemble, clean and reassemble GMAW welder components.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify metals and perform preparation and assembly tasks prior to welding.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Perform and analyze a variety of specified welds, including plug weld, spot weld, butt weld and lap weld.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify the purpose and proper use and fit of personal protective equipment (PPE) required for welding, including eye protection (lens shades), clothing, hearing protection and footwear while identifying the hazards from which they protect individuals.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Ensure all PPE is cleaned appropriately.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas and carry out repairs to straighten metal.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6: Metal Straightening (Core) · Suggested Time: 20-30 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 3

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the range of corrective work procedures required to straighten metal.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Estimate technical measurements to prepare a surface for repair.

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Examine metal to detect how stretched areas feel and look, and determine how to shrink the areas.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the metal to know where to shrink and how much to shrink, and use appropriate tools to shrink the areas.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research, estimate and compare the repair cost to straighten metal versus replacement.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent workplace injuries when straightening metal.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas and carry out repairs to body fill.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Body Filling (Core) · Suggested Time: 8-12 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prepare cost estimates of the materials used to repair damaged surfaces.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Estimate how much body filler and hardener is needed to repair damaged surfaces.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Rough areas to be filled with disc sanders using a 60-or 80-grit disc to ensure the body filler will adhere to the metal.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to spread body filler over damaged areas with putty knives to create a smooth appearance similar to finished panels.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Apply appropriate sanding techniques to prepare surfaces for refinishing and to obtain true panel contours.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine damaged areas for smoothness and adjust as necessary to obtain true panel contours.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Practise proper safety procedures by wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as a particle mask, eye and ear protection and rubber gloves and cleaning as appropriate.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent workplace injuries when body filling.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research short- and long-term health concerns related to body filler particles and dust in the workplace.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas and carry out repairs to flat surfaces.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Flat Panel Repair (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 4 and 5

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prepare cost estimates of the materials used for repairing flat surfaces that have rust damage.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Estimate areas to be cut out for flat panel repairs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to measure areas to produce replacement panels.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Construct repair patches and apply correct welding procedures (e.g., lap joint or butt joint, spot or plug weld).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Select appropriate tools and procedures to prepare work areas for filling.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine patches to ensure repairs are ready for refinishing and painting.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Practise proper safety procedures for welding and using cut-off wheels.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss how repairing rust damage contributes to environmental sustainability.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent workplace injuries when repairing panels.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas and carry out repairs to contoured surfaces.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9: Contoured Surface Repair (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Modules 4 and 5

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prepare cost estimates of the materials used for repairing contoured surfaces.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Estimate areas to be cut out to do contoured panel repairs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Demonstrate how to measure areas and transfer to metal panels, including:
- shaping metal panels to the contour of the areas being replaced;
- constructing repair patches; and,
- applying correct welding procedures (e.g., lap joint or butt joint and spot or plug weld).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine patches to ensure repairs are ready for refinishing and painting.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Estimate how much body filler and hardener is needed to repair damaged surfaces.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Perform appropriate procedures and select appropriate tools to prepare work areas for body filling.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Practice proper safety procedures for welding and using cut-off wheels.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent workplace injuries when repairing contoured panels.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas and carry out surface preparation.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Surface Preparation (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the range of corrective work procedures for surface preparation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Assess the damage and research and prepare an estimate of the cost to prepare surfaces for repair.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify types of material and choose appropriate products and tools following original equipment manufacturer (OEM) specifications.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify various types of plastic and choose compatible materials and tools.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Perform spot repair and surface preparation for metal or plastic surfaces.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop assessment criteria with peers to assess the quality of the repair.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the quality of own and peer’s repair to provide feedback on the strengths and areas for improvement.

outcomes.statement: Estimate the damage and time required to carry out repairs on an automobile.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Estimating Repair Costs (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-12 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Analyze the role of insurance in the autobody trade in Saskatchewan and elsewhere including:
- describing insurance, liability, waiver, total loss, premium, deductible and package policy;
- examining the role and responsibilities of the insurance adjuster/broker, automobile appraiser, automobile owner(s) and autobody repair shop; and,
- comparing original equipment manufacturer (OEM), recycled, remanufactured and after-market parts to repair an automobile.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Estimate damage repair costs including:
- detailed description of all labour operations that must be performed;
- complete list of parts and materials needed for the repair; and,
- total price including labour, parts, materials and applicable taxes.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Interpret technical service bulletins about potential issues that could result in the need for automobile repairs.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine the extent of the damage from outside the automobile and work inward and list everything by section that is bent, broken or missing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify the conditions that make an automobile a total loss.

outcomes.statement: Use and maintain autobody air, hydraulic and electric tools and equipment following safe procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Advanced Tooling (Core) · Suggested Time: 8-12 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 3 and 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the safe use of air, hydraulic and electric tools such as pneumatic chisel, air ratchet, impact wrench, air polisher, air sand blaster, blow gun, air metal shears, power riveter, floor jack, safety stand and hydraulic rams and attachments.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Perform correct procedures when using hand, stationary and power tools for specific autobody repairs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Inspect air, hydraulic and electric tools before use and tag for repair as required.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Maintain and store air, hydraulic and electric tools and equipment appropriately.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Recognize and follow safe work practices when using air, hydraulic and electric tools.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research and estimate the cost to purchase air, hydraulic and electric tools to enter the autobody trade.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas to refinish and repaint parts of an automobile.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Automobile Refinishing and Repainting (Core) · Suggested Time: 15-30 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 12

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Estimate technical measurements and determine appropriate procedures and materials to refinish and repaint parts of an automobile.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Prepare a cost estimate of the materials needed to refinish and repaint parts of an automobile.

indicators.label: c
d
indicators.text: Practice proper safety techniques when using a sandblaster for metal preparation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Apply proper sanding techniques using the appropriate type of sand paper to prepare the surface for painting.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the use of reducers and thinners in autobody repair.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Practice proper techniques and safety procedures to use a spray gun (e.g., siphon and gravity fed), air compressor, air hose and air regulator to paint part or all of an automobile.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Differentiate between the types of spray booths such as a prep station, downdraft, semi-downdraft and cross-draft used in autobody repair.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the purpose and method of application of different types (e.g., epoxy primer, urethane primer surface, polyester primer, urethane sealer and acid etch) of automotive primers.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain the purpose and method of application of different (e.g., acrylic lacquer, acrylic enamel, polyurethane and base coat/clear coat) types of automotive paints.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Apply proper techniques to mask an automobile and describe over-masking and under-masking.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Practise proper safety procedures such as wearing coveralls, rubber gloves and safety glasses and using an appropriate respirator to apply automotive primers, sealers and paints.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Examine the effects of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) on the environment.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Implement a plan to design and organize the workspace to prevent work-related injuries when refinishing and repainting an automobile.

outcomes.statement: Examine the evolution and characteristics of structural components in each section of the automobile.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14: Advanced Automobile Structural Design (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the history of automobile structural design including major changes and characteristics of selected components.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify front (e.g., cowl, shock towers, radiator and supports, fire wall, fenders, hood), centre (e.g., floor pan, pillars, rocker panel, rear shelf, doors, glass, hinges, side impact beam, roof panel, instrument panel, dash) and rear (e.g., trunk floor, trunk lid, quarter panel, lower rear panels, rear shock towers, inner wheel housing, upper body panel) section components of an automobile.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the construction and safety features of plastic bumpers.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify part numbers, prices, installation time and procedures using original equipment manufacturer (OEM) specifications and software and/or manuals.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe proper safety procedures used by certified technicians to disable an automobile air bag sensor system.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine the properties of dissimilar automotive materials (e.g., carbon, fibre, plastic, stainless).

outcomes.statement: Assess complex metal damage and carry out repairs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15: Advanced Metal Repair (Core) · Suggested Time: 15-25 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 6, 7 and 12

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the original point of impact to a panel from a collision to determine potential corrective repairs.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Prepare a cost estimate of the materials used for metal repair.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate proper use of hand and power tools to contour metal.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify all direct and indirect damage to panels.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Remove glass and trim, if needed, before attempting to straighten metal.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Remove damage from the least damaged area to the worst damaged area.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Determine the amount of body filler needed to repair damage.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Repair major damage using picking tools, dent pullers, uni-spot pullers, body spoons, suction cups and hydraulic rams.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Inspect repair and carry out adjustments as necessary to complete repair.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Recognize and follow safe work practices when using hand and power tools.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Implement a plan to design and organize the workspace to prevent work-related injuries related to metal repair.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Examine the effects of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) on the environment.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Investigate and describe short- and long-term health concerns related to body filling products and dust in the workplace.

outcomes.statement: Assess panel misalignment issues and carry out repairs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16: Panel Alignment (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 3 and 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the range of corrective work procedures that may be required to align a panel.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine panel misalignment issues (e.g., vertical misalignment, loose latches, hinges) that require corrective action.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Prepare a cost estimate to align a panel.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the appropriate corrective action and tools to align a panel (e.g., hood, door, trunk lid, fender, quarter panel).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Determine proper measurements for panel alignment.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate proper use of hand and power tools to align panels.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Recognize and follow safe work practices when using appropriate hand and power tools to align panels.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Assess the design and organization of the workspace to prevent workplace injuries when conducting panel alignment.

outcomes.statement: Analyze types and functions of automobile glass and carry out glass repairs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17: Glass Removal and Installation (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 3 and 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the different types (e.g., laminated and tempered) of glass and their purpose in an automobile.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research legislation related to approved automotive glass materials.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine glass damage (e.g., circular bullseyes, linear cracks, crack chips, dings, pits and star-shaped breaks), location of damage (e.g., inside of windshield, deep damage to both layers of glass, complex multiple cracks, very long cracks, contaminated or edge cracks) and identify appropriate tools, materials and procedures to conduct glass repairs.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare the advantages and disadvantages of using original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and aftermarket automobile glass in repair.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Determine required procedures to remove and install glass in an automobile.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate appropriate use of hand and power tools to repair glass (e.g., windshield, sidelite and backlite).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Practise correct safety procedures such as wearing gloves, long sleeved apparel and eye protection when repairing glass.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate issues and potential solutions related to recycling automotive glass.

outcomes.statement: Examine the evolution of automobile air bags and associated sensors.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18: Air Bags (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the location and function of the components of an automobile air bag system.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the evolution of air bag systems in automobiles, including increased safety achieved through each improved design.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe “safing” and arming sensors to ensure deployment of an air bag when a collision is severe enough to warrant it.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe how certified technicians disarm an air bag system prior to repair and re-arm air bag systems when finished a repair.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Propose an innovative air bag system, including considerations such as automobile type, rate of deployment, placement of air bag system, laws of motion and injury prevention to automobile occupants.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Compare legislation related to air bags in Saskatchewan with other Canadian jurisdictions.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe how automobiles are certified to be road safe after a collision.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore the advantages and disadvantages of turning on and off automobile air bag sensors.

outcomes.statement: Assess the interior and exterior condition of an automobile and apply detailing procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 19: Automobile Detailing (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Analyze the interior and exterior condition of an automobile to identify required detailing procedures.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Complete interior (e.g., vacuuming, brushing, steam cleaning, glass cleaning, leather trimming, re-vacuuming, wiping, perfuming) and exterior (e.g., washing, drying, claying, polishing, sealing) detailing of an automobile in addition to:
- inspecting the glass and completing necessary repairs;
- cleaning the chrome with appropriate products; and,
- inspecting the headlight and turn signal glass, light bulbs and completing necessary repairs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Analyze operational complications such as the heating and air conditioning (HVAC) system, stained switches and hazy windows on the interior of the automobile in addition to:
- inspecting the interior and removing after-market attachments that are loose or worn;
- inspecting the carpet and seats for rips, tears and stains (e.g., soil, grease, chocolate, oil, candy, road tar or blood) and completing necessary repairs; and,
- inspecting the door and window weather stripping and completing necessary repairs.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine the appropriate materials, costs and tools to detail the interior and exterior of the automobile.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the environmental effects of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) used in detailing.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine short- and long-term health concerns related to chemical exposure and demonstrate the appropriate safety procedures when using chemicals.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas and carry out repairs to automobile trim.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 20: Automobile Trim Removal and Installation (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 3 and 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify areas of automobile trim needing repair.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Prepare a cost estimate to remove and replace trim.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text:
Identify interior and exterior trim materials and fastening systems (e.g., clips, adhesives, screws) and carry out the process to repair trim including:
- removing door panels and upholstery parts to access fasteners;
- removing vinyl, overlays and decals; and,
- removing weather stripping from all areas of the automobile and installing new materials.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine an automobile and adjust and service trim accessories as needed.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate appropriate use of hand and power tools to remove and install trim.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Practice correct safety procedures such as wearing gloves, long sleeved apparel and eye protection when repairing trim.

outcomes.statement: Analyze plastics in automobile design and carry out plastic repairs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 21: Plastic Repair (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Compare different types of plastics (i.e., thermoplastic olefin (TPO), thermo-set, sheet molding compound (SMC), polypropylene) commonly used in automotive construction.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the role of plastic in the manufacturing of automobiles.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify types of plastics by grinding or locating ISO codes in damaged areas before proceeding with plastic repair.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the range of corrective procedures that may be required to repair plastic.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research, estimate and compare the cost to replace versus to repair plastic components (e.g., bumper repair) in automobile repair.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Conduct a plastic repair to, or above, original equipment manufacturer (OEM) specifications.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss different processes and adhesives (e.g., plastic welding, bonding) to repair damage to plastic components.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate trends in plastic use and the potential impact of electric automobiles on plastic consumption.

outcomes.statement: Assess complex corrosion damage to refinish and repaint part of an automobile.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 22: Automotive Refinishing and Painting (Optional) · Suggested Time: 45-55 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 10 and 12

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine the cause of corrosion damage and select the appropriate products and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) procedures to protect against corrosion.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Prepare a cost estimate of the materials required to refinish and repaint an automobile.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Select appropriate tools, such as a spray gun, and appropriate techniques to perform basic surface preparation.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Practise correct safety procedures such as wearing overalls and safety goggles and using a respirator.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Practise proper safety procedures following WHMIS 2015 specifications.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe effects of collision repair and refinishing technology on human health and well-being, including tradespersons working in the field and those who use their services.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine collision repair and refinishing technology’s sustainability practices and impact on the environment.

outcomes.statement: Examine the evolution and characteristics of aluminum in automobile design.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 23: Aluminum Repair (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the evolution and use of aluminum in automobile design.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the composition (e.g., aluminum alloys, magnesium alloys) and grading of aluminum in automobile applications.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify aluminum repair techniques (e.g., welding, riveting, bonding) according to original equipment manufacturer (OEM) specifications.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe appropriate surface preparation procedures and appropriate tools for aluminum repair.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Determine appropriate corrosion protection products according to OEM specifications.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore career opportunities in aluminum repair (e.g., fishing boats and travel trailers/motorhomes).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate current and future carbon footprints of aluminum in automobile design.

outcomes.statement: Examine the evolution and characteristics of alternative fuel automobiles.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 24: Alternative Fuel Automobiles (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the evolution of alternate fuel automobiles (e.g., full electric, hybrid, hydrogen, propane, natural gas) and characteristics of selected models.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine safety concerns with alternate fuel automobiles and the autobody trade.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research insurance industry claims related to alternate fuel automobiles, including total loss.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create, using drawing skills, computer-aided design programs or model-making, an innovative alternative fuel automobile considering factors such as new technologies, type of alternative fuel, fuel system integrity, protective barriers, occupant and autobody repairer safety and cost efficiency.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop assessment criteria in consultation with peers and instructor to assess an innovative fuel automobile design.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss own and peer’s alternate fuel automobile designs to provide feedback on the strengths and areas for improvement.

outcomes.statement: Examine the evolution and characteristics of electrical and electronic systems in automobile design.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 25: Introduction to Automobile Electrical and Electronic Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the history and evolution of electrical and electronic systems in automobile design including major changes and characteristics of selected components.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain electron theory, Ohm’s Law and automotive circuits in automobile electrical and electronic systems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the characteristics of automotive storage batteries and their relationship to the electrical components of an automobile.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify and repair automotive wiring, electrical and electronic components and computer components related to collision repair.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine an automobile to identify which sensors have to be disconnected, tested and reconnected during a repair process.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate basic diagnostic issues and research the range of corrective work procedures to repair electrical and electronic system failures in automobiles.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Perform correct safety procedures and the appropriate use of hand and power tools to disconnect and reconnect sensors.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore information technologies (e.g., databases, diagnostic software) used in the autobody industry.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the use of complex materials, construction and technologies in automobile design.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 26: Automobile Collision Technology (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the evolution of complex materials (e.g., high-strength steel, lightweight materials), construction (e.g., exterior crumples in a collision) and technologies (e.g., safety sensors) in automobile design and the impact on autobody repair.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore information technologies (e.g., databases, diagnostic software, estimating programs) used in the autobody industry.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research and estimate the cost of purchasing electrical testing equipment to enter the autobody trade.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine upcoming technologies, trends and processes (e.g., bonding, welding, finishing) in the autobody trade.

outcomes.statement: Examine materials and processes used to weld aluminum.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 27: Aluminum Welding (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research different types of aluminum alloys commonly used in automotive construction.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare processes and techniques used for aluminum and steel welding.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research effects of contamination on aluminum surfaces.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate issues and potential solutions related to welding aluminum.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine upcoming technologies, trends and processes for aluminum welding in the autobody trade.

outcomes.statement: Apply principles of colour theory and tinting to correct common paint problems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 28: Colour Theory (Optional) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the basic concepts of colour theory and how different lighting affects colour perception.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare metallic, pearlescent and tri-coat types of paint.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe and apply mixing variants to colour match original factory paint.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Perform a colour tinting to obtain a blendable match for a test panel.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss own and peer’s colour matching to provide feedback on the strengths and areas for improvement.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore reasons refinish colours may not match the original automobile colour.

outcomes.statement: Assess damaged areas by measuring automobile body dimensions.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 29: Measurement (Optional) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the history of measurement devices used in autobody repair.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify types of specialized measuring equipment and apply the appropriate procedures to use measuring equipment in autobody repair.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate the concept of “XYZ” coordinates (X = length, Y = width and Z = height) of each control point to verify accuracy.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe “point to point” measurements and use appropriate equipment to gauge the automobile’s reference point.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research, estimate and compare the cost to repair a frame versus replacement.

outcomes.statement: Analyze responsibilities of individuals and businesses when selling or purchasing automobiles.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 30: Buying or Selling an Automobile (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Describe the responsibility of sellers when selling automobiles including the ethical and legal implications of selling used automobiles.

outcomes.printedWith: Module 31: Personal Skills for Success (Optional) · Suggested Time: 1-2 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create a resume or a skills list.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Determine and practise guidelines used to participate in interviews.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research employability skills to be successful in the workplace.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate essential skills for the workplace and identify which would be most important for a career in autobody.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Establish a relationship with others in the workplace or shop setting by clearly defining roles and using effective communication.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Develop an awareness of cultural diversity and its importance in the workplace.

outcomes.statement: Explore autobody-related occupations.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 70: Careers in Autobody (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create a list of personal interests, skills and traits that could lead to a career in the autobody trade.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate occupations in the autobody trade (e.g., autobody repair technician, automotive restoration technician, commercial vehicle body repairer, automotive detailer, damage repair appraiser, automotive painter and insurance estimator).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research which autobody-related occupations are facing shortages and which are oversubscribed locally, regionally or provincially.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the roles, responsibilities, educational qualifications and personal and professional qualities common to people involved in autobody-related jobs.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Explore opportunities for underrepresented populations in the automotive industry.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Communicate research findings related to autobody occupations through a display, brochure, video, presentation software, website or an oral presentation.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a plan to attain a job of one’s choice in the autobody trade.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify entrepreneurial opportunities available in the autobody trade.

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80A: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s performance during the interview.
