indicators.text: Describe the emotional requirements of the patient diagnosed with dementia.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine the role of the family in the care of the patient diagnosed with dementia.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Research the impact of caring for family members with dementia on primary caregivers.

outcomes.statement: Investigate ways to support mental health of adults in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 54: Mental Health in Health Care Environments (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research one or more mental health disorders such as acquired brain injuries, anxiety, depressive disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorders, schizophrenia spectrum disorders and trauma and stressor-related disorders.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine causes, signs and symptoms of depression.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss care strategies to support patients with depression.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe how to support patients with mental health disorders.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify factors that may contribute to mental health disorders (e.g., biological factors, childhood experiences, stressful life events, diet).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the effects of mental health disorders on families (e.g., guilt, blame, finances).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate local adult community mental health services.

outcomes.statement: Recognize the importance of exercise and activity for patients on bed rest.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 55: Exercise and Activity for Patients on Bed Rest (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe reasons why patients may require bed rest.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate among different types of bed rest (e.g., strict bed rest, bed rest with commode privileges, bed rest with bathroom privileges).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explore the complications of bed rest (e.g., contracture, muscle atrophy, hypotension) and how to prevent them (e.g., moving the patient every two hours).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize the devices (e.g., bed boards, foot boards, trochanter rolls, splints, trapeze) used to support and maintain body alignment.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate a personal range of motion exercises (e.g., abduction, adduction, extension, flexion, hyperextension, rotation).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore range of motion activities that could be offered in long-term care facilities for full-time wheelchair users.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the social and emotional benefits of exercise and activity for patients on bed rest.

outcomes.statement: Observe how to position, transfer and lift a patient.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 56: Transfers and Lifts (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate different types of bed positions (e.g., Fowler’s position, supine position, lateral position, Sim’s position, prone position, sitting position).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify positioning requirements in a care plan directive.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize tools (e.g., fan-folded turning pad, slider sheet, transfer belt, transfer board) used to move a patient safely.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate programs and services that provide training for transfers, lifts, and repositioning (e.g., Transferring, Lifting and Repositioning training).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research frequent injuries (e.g., back, shoulder and psychological injuries) for health care providers related to lifts and transfers.

outcomes.statement: Recognize the importance of personal hygiene in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 57: Personal Hygiene (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the importance of personal hygiene for patients and care providers in health care environments.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine daily care routines including morning care, afternoon care and evening care.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how to assist with personal hygiene while considering the patient’s dignity, independence, individualized care, preferences, privacy and safety.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe oral hygiene and the observations to report to the care team.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine ways to support good oral health.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the labelling process for personal items (e.g., clothing, glasses, blankets, dentures) in health care environments.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the guidelines for bathing (e.g., collect all needed items before the bath, provide for privacy, protect from burns and scalds).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe compassionate caring for the patient receiving assistance with bathing.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify the safety precautions for patients taking tub baths or showers.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine safe practices for caregivers providing personal hygiene services.

outcomes.statement: Investigate infection prevention strategies.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 58: Infection Prevention (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the signs and symptoms of infection (e.g., fever and chills, nausea, rash).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine ways in which microbes are transmitted (e.g., the chain of infection) and steps to limit transmission.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss risk factors for infection (e.g., stress, poor nutrition, lack of sleep).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify routine immunizations for infection prevention.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate proper handwashing, cleaning and disinfection techniques.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate donning and doffing of personal protective equipment (e.g., masks, gloves, gowns).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Investigate the risks to supportive care providers and patients when infection control is not adhered to (e.g., spread of disease to a more compromised population).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research disease outbreaks including pandemic and epidemic diseases that have had significant effects on the general population past and present.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe the role and responsibilities supportive care providers in preventing the spread of infection.

outcomes.statement: Examine safety measures and procedures in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 59: Safety Measures and Procedures in Health Care (Core for Supportive Care Focus) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 4

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: List the risk factors for incidents (e.g., distracted or fatigued caregivers, medication, age, patients with vision, hearing or mobility challenges).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe how the proper use of specialized equipment (e.g., call bells, bed rails, hand rails) can promote patient safety.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the safety measures to prevent falls, poisoning, suffocation and burns in older adults.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate health care codes that support safety (e.g., code red, blue, burgundy, white).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe guidelines to follow for emergency preparedness (e.g., in case of fire, weather event, lock down) in a health care environment.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe safety guidelines to follow when using electrical equipment such as hair dryers, curling irons and electric razors with patients in health care environments.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain household management safety, including guidelines for dealing with pest infestations, linen and light housekeeping.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain the protocol to dispose of contaminated items or waste, including sharp objects.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe measures to ensure personal safety when at work in a health care environment (e.g., when entering a patient’s home, choice of clothing and jewelry).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explore the risks associated with working alone with a patient and how they can be mitigated.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe the steps to reporting a workplace injury.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Explain how various emotions and reactions may block effective responses.

outcomes.statement: Apply bed making techniques.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 60: Bed Making (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain how to handle linen according to the rules of standard practice (e.g., frequency of changes, order of application to bed, manipulation of the linen).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: List the types of bed linens used when making a patient’s bed.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize the different types of incontinence pads (e.g., reusable, disposable).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe safety measures for bed making.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the differences between open beds (i.e., shortly before the bed is to be occupied), closed beds (i.e., expected to be unoccupied for several hours or days) and occupied beds (i.e., a bed being made while the patient is in the bed).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate the making of an open and a closed bed.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate grooming and dressing strategies.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 61: Grooming and Dressing (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the importance of hair care and shaving.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the factors that affect hair care.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize conditions that may be related to a patient’s hair care plan such as alopecia, dandruff and pediculosis.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how to care for matted and tangled hair.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss how to provide culturally sensitive grooming.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe how to shampoo hair.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: List the steps to shave a patient.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify safety considerations related to basic nail care.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Research training opportunities to learn about appropriate nail and foot care procedures.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Experiment with applying makeup or styling hair on another person according to their wishes.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe how to dress and undress patients, including patients with intravenous tubing.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Identify proper care of wigs (e.g., storage, washing, drying).

outcomes.statement: Explain ways to promote patient comfort and sleep.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 62: Patient Comfort (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize that comfort is personal to each person and based on past experiences.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify elements in a room that promote patient well-being (e.g., temperature, ventilation, odors, noise, lighting, feelings of safety).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe why comfort and well-being are important.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain why rest and sleep are important.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify factors that affect sleep (e.g., illness, nutrition, exercise, medications).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss ways to address social and emotional needs of patients winding down to sleep (e.g., spending time, talking with patients).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Suggest care plan measures that promote sleep (e.g., comfortable room temperature, clean linens, darkened room, bed positioning).

outcomes.statement: Examine common chronic conditions.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 63: Chronic Conditions (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe common chronic illnesses.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Categorize chronic conditions according to body systems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the relationship between chronic pain and chronic conditions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare acute pain and chronic pain.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the effects of chronic pain on quality of life.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the concept of compassionate caring for a patient with a chronic condition and pain.

outcomes.statement: Explore nutrition, fluids and intravenous therapy in health care environments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 64A: Nutrition in Health Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the principles of Canada’s Food Guide, including Canada’s Dietary Guidelines.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the structure and purpose of food labels.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss how nutrient requirements change throughout the life cycle.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify adult fluid requirements.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify factors that affect food choice and nutrition (e.g., personal choice, culinary culture, allergies, finances).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine the social, emotional and cultural importance of meals and meal planning.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Research local meal delivery services such as Meal on Wheels.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain why food safety is important (e.g., food storage, preparation and serving practices).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe special diets (e.g., sodium-controlled diets, diabetic diets, heart healthy) and why they are necessary.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine the purpose of enteral nutrition (e.g., a nutritional formula delivered into the gastrointestinal tract with a tube).

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe the purpose of intravenous therapy (e.g., to provide needed fluids, to reverse dehydration in the body, to replace minerals and vitamins).

outcomes.statement: Examine the supportive care provider’s role in meal planning and feeding patients.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 64B: Nutrition in Health Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 64A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the role of the supportive care provider in meal planning and preparation (e.g., planning menus, grocery shopping, supporting special cultural dietary practices).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe how to create a pleasant patient-centered dining environment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate special eating utensils available for patients with motricity issues (e.g., curved forks, special grips, plate guards).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how to feed patients, including patients who may have chewing difficulties, swallowing difficulty, vision impairments.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate feeding another person (e.g., ask them what they prefer to eat, what they would like to eat first and when they want to drink).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the supportive care provider’s role in assisting with intravenous therapy.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Plan a meal for a fictional patient with specific nutritional or cultural requirements.

outcomes.statement: Examine urinary and bowel elimination care.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 65: Elimination (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the characteristics of normal urine.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Summarize the guidelines for maintaining normal urinary elimination (e.g., provide fluids as instructed by the care plan, help the patient to the bathroom when requested).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe urinary incontinence and the care it requires (e.g., provide dry garments and linens, decrease fluid intake before bedtime, use incontinence products).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain why catheters are used.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe normal stools and the normal pattern and frequency of bowel movements.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify factors that affect bowel elimination.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the measures that promote comfort and safety during defecation.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain why enemas or suppositories are given.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Recognize how to collect urine and stool samples.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss why urine and stools specimens are collected.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe compassionate caring for the patient receiving assistance with elimination.

outcomes.statement: Explore adult hearing, vision, speech and language disorders.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 66: Adult Hearing, Vision and Speech (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the signs of hearing impairment (e.g., speaking too loudly, leaning forward to hear, responding inappropriately).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe possible effects of hearing impairment (e.g., a change in behaviour, speech challenges, frustration when communicating, increase in other senses).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine aids for patients with vision impairments (e.g., eyeglasses, contact lenses, Braille).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify communication aids and how they assist patients (e.g., communication boards, electronic devices, voice amplifier, emergency alert button).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the emotional effects of a language disorder (e.g., anger, stress, shame).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss how to care for patients with speech and language disorders as an supportive care providers (e.g., be mindful of non-verbal communication, be alert for signs of fatigue, reduce surrounding distractions).

outcomes.statement: Explore childhood development disorders and disabilities requiring the support of a supportive care provider.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 67: Supporting Childhood Developmental Disorders (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify causes and effects of common developmental disorders and disabilities (e.g., Autism Spectrum Disorder, Down Syndrome, Cerebral Palsy).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss how common developmental disorders and disabilities affect physical, social-emotional and intellectual function.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the impact a developmental disorder or disability can have on children and their families.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore how children with developmental disorders are included in public school settings (e.g., transportation, in the classroom, during meals).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate the relationship between public education and health care systems that support children with developmental disorders and disabilities.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe how to care for young students with developmental disorders and disabilities in schools and in personal homes.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Assess the accessibility of a variety of indoor and outdoor community spaces (e.g., playgrounds, public libraries).

outcomes.statement: Recognize signs of abuse, bullying and harassment in a health care environment.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 68: Abuse in Health Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the types of abuse (e.g., physical abuse, sexual abuse, emotional abuse, financial abuse, neglect).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify signs of abuse (e.g., physical injuries, a change in behaviour, unpaid bills, lack of personal hygiene).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe possible types of spousal abuse, child abuse and abuse of older persons.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine how people with intellectual disabilities may be vulnerable to abuse in health care environments.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Recognize types of abuse of patients (e.g., rough handling, isolation) and health care workers (e.g., name calling, cultural slurs, physical attacks).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain how to respond to abusive patient behaviour.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain the supportive care provider’s responsibilities when reporting abuse in a health care environment.

outcomes.statement: Examine ways to provide end of life care.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 69: End of Life Care (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-4 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define palliative care.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Recognize that personal beliefs, culture and religion influence practices and attitudes about death.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine Kübler-Ross’s five stages of grief (e.g., denial, anger, bargaining, depression and acceptance).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore how to support the emotional, social, intellectual, spiritual and physical needs of a dying patient as a supportive care provider.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify the roles and responsibilities of each member of the palliative care team.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate legal issues surrounding death and dying such as advance directives, do not resuscitate orders and medical assistance in dying.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine post-mortem care, including the possible responsibilities of the supportive care provider (e.g., may involve repositioning the body, cleaning soiled areas).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research death rituals and practices from different cultural and religious groups.

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80A: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III – Occupational Health and Safety in The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019:
- the right to know – the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate – in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse – work that you believe is unusually dangerous.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s performance during the interview.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the contributions that small businesses make to the local and Saskatchewan economy.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of operating a small business, including a home-based business.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the advantages and disadvantages of owning a sole proprietorship, partnership and/or franchise business.

indicators.label: d

indicators.label: e

outcomes.statement: Analyze and explore earth-science related career paths in Saskatchewan, Canada and the world.
outcomes.printedWith: CP, DM

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Generate a list of occupations that require a background in earth science through research and/or participation in events such as a career fair or job shadow. (K, S)

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore the connection between topics in Earth Science 30 and occupations of personal interest. (S, A, STSE)

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify which earth-science related occupations are facing shortages and which are oversubscribed locally, regionally and/or nationally. (STSE, S, K, A)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine the roles, responsibilities, educational qualifications and personal and professional qualities common to people involved in earth-science related jobs. (S, A)

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compare the roles and responsibilities of various earth science professionals as they engage with a specific project. (K, STSE, A)

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine the role of regulatory (e.g., Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Saskatchewan [APEGS]) and non-regulatory (e.g., Saskatchewan Geological Survey, Saskatchewan Mining Association, anadian Geophysical Union and the Canadian Water Resources Association) bodies that support earth scientists. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Participate in, and reflect on, an earth-science related field experience. (K, A)

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Communicate research findings related to earth science occupations through a display, brochure, video, presentation software, website or orally. (K, S, A, STSE)

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Use acquired knowledge to develop a plan to attain a job of personal interest in the earth science field. (S, A)

outcomes.statement: Create and carry out a plan to explore a topic covered in Earth Science 30 in depth.
outcomes.printedWith: CP, DM, SI, TPS

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Design a scientific investigation related to a topic of study in Earth Science 30that includes a testable question, a hypothesis, an experimental design that will test the hypothesis and detailed procedures for collecting and analyzing data. (STSE, S)

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Carry out an experiment following established scientific protocols to investigate a question of interest related to one or more of the topics of Earth Science 30. (S, A, K, STSE)

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assemble and reflect on a portfolio that demonstrates an understanding of a topic of interest related to biology. (S, A)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Participate in and reflect on a field experience related to one or more topics of Earth Science 30. (S)

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Design, construct and evaluate the effectiveness of a device, model or technique that demonstrates the scientific principles underlying concept related to an Earth Science 30 topic. (STSE, S)

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Debate an issued related to earth science, including developing materials to support the arguments for and arguments against a position. (A, K, S).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Share the results of student-directed research through a display, presentation, performance, demonstration, song, game, commercial, fine art representation, video or research paper. (S)

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Construct a tool (e.g., rubric, checklist, self-evaluation form or peer-evaluation form) to assess the process and products involved in a student-directed study. (S, A)

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Consider natural disasters in the news and discuss causes of these phenomena and their impacts on the human environment and natural environment. (S, STSE, A)

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Produce a profile of the earth beneath their feet by locating oneself on the geological profile of Saskatchewan and relating this to the geological history of your area. (S, A)

outcomes.statement: Examine the multi-disciplinary nature of earth science.
outcomes.printedWith: SI, DM

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Construct a representation of the major fields of earth science and the major topics of study within each field. (S, STSE, A)

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between the characteristics of the four major Earth spheres (i.e., atmosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and lithosphere). (K, STSE)

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss why earth scientists consider interactions between and within two or more of Earth's spheres when they study earth processes. (STSE)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Outline possible interactions between two or more of Earth's spheres within the context of a particular event and/or issue. (S)

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine why earth scientists utilize a systems approach by considering boundaries, inputs, outputs and feedback loops when investigating an earth science issue. (STSE, S, A)

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Provide examples of how earth scientists collect evidence using analytical, field, theoretical, experimental and/or modeling studies. (STSE)

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify how earth scientists draw upon principles and processes from scientific fields such as biology, chemistry, computer science, geology, mathematics, and physics in order to address their questions. (STSE)

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Identify issues and events in Saskatchewan that might be studied from an earth science perspective. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Recognize how historical and contemporary observations, including those made by First Nations and Métis peoples, can contribute to a greater understanding of Earth's processes. (STSE, A)

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Assess how earth science processes and principles are applicable to the study of other planets and celestial bodies. (STSE, S)

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Identify the significance of contributions made by Canadians to the field of earth science. (K, STSE)

outcomes.statement: Examine the evidence for and the importance of plate tectonics theory in explaining the processes that produced Earth's major surface features.
outcomes.printedWith: SI

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of plate tectonics as the unifying concept in earth science. (STSE)

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the key principles and driving forces of plate tectonics theory including how the theory subsumes ideas related to continental drift. (K)

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the development of the continental drift hypothesis, including the evidence (e.g., fossil, mineral, ancient climates and continental shape) scientists used to support this hypothesis. (K, S, STSE)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the scientific belief that the movement of tectonic plates was responsible for the formation and break up of continents (e.g., Pangea, Rodinia and Gondwana) over geological time. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the formation of geological features (e.g., ocean trenches, mid-ocean ridges, transform faults, mountain ranges and island arcs) associated with convergent, divergent and transform boundaries, with referenceto the asthenosphere, lithosphere and mantle convection. (K)

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Correlate the world distribution of mountain ranges, volcanoes and earthquakes with the location, boundaries and movement of lithospheric plates. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Model the movement of lithospheric plates over geologic time and relate this to the geologic history of Saskatchewan. (S)

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Analyze data,using tools such as satellite photos and the Global Positioning System (GPS),to determine the rate of relative lithospheric plate motion. (S)

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Predict the locations of future plate boundaries based on current lithospheric plate movement rates and compare with scientific predictions. (S)

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Consider which celestial bodies (e.g., Mars, Europa and exoplanets) could have or could not have geological features that might be explained by plate tectonics. (K)

outcomes.statement: Analyze how geologiests use the fossil record and relative and absolute dating methods to determine the geological history of Earth and to construct the geologic time scale.
outcomes.printedWith: SI

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss why geologists consider the geologic time scale as an important framework for understanding changes to Earth's crust, life forms, climate and continental positions over time. (K)

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain how the paradigm shift from catastrophism to uniformitarianism has influenced scientific thinking about Earth's geological history. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess the importance of the fossil record as evidence to support scientific understanding of geological time and evolution. (STSE, A, K)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize that the nomenclature (e.g., eon, era, period and epoch) and major divisions of the geologic time scale are based on scientists' interpretation of the fossil record. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Outline the major geological and biological events that occurred during a particular eon, era, period or epoch of the geologic time scale. (S)

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research the consequences of catastrophic events such as asteroid impacts (at Cretaceous-Tertiary [K-T] boundary in Saskatchewan), glaciation and volcanism on the fossil record. (K, S, STSE)

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Contrast absolute and relative dating principles and techniques and the benefits of each. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Provide examples of the key concepts of relative dating, including the law of superposition, principle of uniformitarianism, principle of original horizontality, principle of cross-cutting relationships, principle of inclusions and components, principle of faunal succession, principle of lateral continuity, and unconformities. (S, K)

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe how and why scientists use radiometric dating techniques to determine the absolute age of rocks. (S, K)

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Contrast absolute and relative dating principles and techniques and the benefits of each. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Discuss how scientists revise the geologic time scale in response to new geological and fossil evidence. (STSE)

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Provide examples that show geologists can learn about Earth's formation and early history by studying other objects in the solar system. (STSE, A)

outcomes.statement: Analyze the composition of Earth's atmosphere and factors that influence changes in the composition in the short and long term.
outcomes.printedWith: SI

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the history of Earth's atmosphere, including the origins and sources of nitrogen, oxygen and other gases (e.g., argon, carbon dioxide, neon, helium and methane) and the composition of those gases in today's atmosphere. (K, S)

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Model the role of atmospheric layers in insulating Earth and protecting Earth's surface from extra-terrestrial dangers such as ultraviolet light, solar wind and meteors. (K)

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate how factors such as the oxygen and carbon dioxide balance in the oceans influence the composition of Earth's atmosphere. (K)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how earth scientists use data such as ice composition, tree growth, sedimentary content and landforms to infer the composition of ancient climates. (STSE)

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the characteristics of notable climatic events (e.g., volcanic activity, Great Oxygenation Event, Snowball Earth events and asteroid collisions) in Earth's history, the impacts of those events on the composition of the atmosphere and their correlation with the fossil and rock record. (S, STSE)

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate the function and operation of various technologies (e.g., Earth orbiting satellites, drones, weather balloons, rocketsondes and radiosondes) used to gather data about the composition of the atmosphere. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Determine, using archived data, whether the frequency and severity of extreme weather events (e.g., tornadoes, hurricanes and blizzards) is changing locally, nationally and globally. (S, STSE)

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine the effects of El Niño and La Niña on Saskatchewan and predict their effects on future seasons based on historical data. (K, S, STSE)

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Hypothesize what changes were present or would need to occur to other planet's atmospheres in order to sustain life on those planets. (STSE)

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Recognize that methane measurements in Mars may provide evidence of anaerobic bacteria similar to those found on Earth. (K)

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Relate terrestrial observations of storms to similar storms on the gas giant planets. (STSE, A)

outcomes.statement: Investigate the characteristics of the hydrosphere and how hydrospheric processes impact the atmosphere, biosphere and lithosphere.
outcomes.printedWith: SI, DM

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Outline the distribution of the hydrosphere in groundwater, surface water, oceans, glaciers and the atmosphere. (S, K)

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the types of evidence scientists gather to determine if water is or was present on other planets and celestial bodies. (STSE)

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the technologies (e.g., acoustics, imaging, buoys and underwater vehicles) and processes scientists use to learn about the hydrosphere. (STSE, S)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate how factors such as porosity and permeability influence the storage and movement of groundwater. (S, K, STSE)

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Model the movement of groundwater, including the locations of reservoirs and flows, in a hypothetical or actual groundwater system. (S, K, A)

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Provide examples of how groundwater works as an erosional agent, resulting in Karst topographic features such as sinkholes and caverns. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine how groundwater storage and flow, along with the depth of the water table, are key considerations affecting the location and maintenance of buildings and infrastructure, including drinking water supplies. (K)

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Provide examples of the ways in which rivers and streams erode, transport and deposit sediment to shape stream valleys and create depositional landforms such as deltas, levees and alluvial fans. (K)

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Examine the importance of glaciers in the hydrologic cycle and Earth's climate. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Consider how extended periods of glaciation, including potential Snowball Earth events, have impacted feedback loops related to the biosphere and other components of the geosphere. (K)

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Explore how Earth's oceans affect climate through heat storage and transfer. (K)

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Correlate the locations of the large wind-driven surface ocean currents and thermohaline circulation on Earth. (S, K)

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Describe the ways in which changes in factors such as ocean salinity, ocean temperature and surface winds influence the processes of ocean convection and thermohaline circulation. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Examine the impacts of climate change on the ability of oceans to moderate temperature, absorb carbon dioxide and resist acidification. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Examine the role of governmental and non-governmental organizations in studying the effects of human activities on one or more components of the hydrosphere. (S, STSE, A)

outcomes.statement: Examine the processes that lead to the formation of sedimentary, igneous and metamorphic rocks and minerals.
outcomes.printedWith: SI

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Pose scientific questions about the characteristics and formation of rocks and minerals. (S, STSE)

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the characteristics geologists use to determine whether an Earth material is a mineral. (K, A)

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare the three primary methods of mineral formation (i.e., precipitation of mineral matter, crystallization of molten rock and deposition resulting from biological processes). (S, K)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Observe and classify mineral samples using standard physical properties (e.g., cleavage, fracture, crystal form, hardness, lustre, colour, magnetism and streak). (S, STSE)

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Differentiate among the three main rock groups (i.e., igneous, sedimentary, igneous and metamorphic) by their processes of formation, including the roles of time, heat and pressure. (K)

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Outline the basic transitions inherent in the rock cycle, and the forces that disrupt equilibrium to cause these transitions. (K, A)

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Classify igneous rocks according to criteria such as method of formation (i.e., intrusive or extrusive) and mineral composition (e.g., felsic or mafic). (K)

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain how geologists can infer how an igneous rock was formed by examining its texture (i.e., intrusive or extrusive). (K, STSE)

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe how the general mechanisms of mechanical and chemical weathering processes, erosion and deposition contribute to the development of sedimentary rocks. (K, A)

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Compare the major features of continental, marine and transitional depositional (sedimentary) environments through structures such as grain size, bedding, ripple marks, mud cracks and fossils in various sedimentary rock formations. (S, K)

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe how the agents of metamorphism (i.e., heat, pressure, directional stress and chemically active fluids) influence the formation of metamorphic rocks. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Compare the characteristics of foliated and non-foliated metamorphic rocks. (K, S)

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Explain why locations where igneous activity and metamorphic rocks occur correlate with plate boundaries and plate movement. (K, STSE, A)

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Correlate the location and composition of depositional layers to major events such as volcanic eruptions, glaciation, flooding, mountain building and metamorphism. (K)

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Create, and validate with the help of others, a resource such as a field guide for a specific mineral or rock group. (S, A)

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Research the ways in which society makes use of sedimentary, igneous and metamorphic rocks for various purposes such as art, architecture, industrial materials and energy resources including petroleum, natural gas, potash and uranium. (STSE, S, A)

outcomes.statement: Investigate the processes and technologies used to locate and extract mineral resources and fossil fuels locally, provincially and globally.
outcomes.printedWith: DM, SI, TPS

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the location, method of extraction, uses and economic impact of major fossil fuel and mineral (e.g., gold, diamond, rare earth elements, copper, zinc, kaolin, coal, potash, uranium, sodium, sulfate and salt) resources locally, provincially and/or globally. (STSE)

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the surface and sub-surface geologic features associated with major mineral (e.g., gold, diamond, rare earth elements, copper, zinc, kaolin, potash, uranium, sodium sulfate and salt), building stone, aggregate and fossil fuel resources of Saskatchewan. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate how depositional setting and geologic history influencesthe location of major mineral and fossil fuel resources in Saskatchewan. (K)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Contrast the operation and utility of different imaging methods (e.g., satellite imaging, gravity, magnetics, electromagnetics and seismic) used to locate hard rock and soft rock resource deposits. (K)

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify anomalies from geophysical surveys and geologic maps and relate them to structural features and associated resource deposits. (S)

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain how geologists use applications of seismic body waves (i.e., longitudinal p-wave and transverse s-wave), surface waves and the laws of reflection and refraction to determine the presence and position of economically useful geological deposits. (K)

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Model a seismic survey using tools such as a ultrasonic motion detector. (S)

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Recognize the importance of obtaining surface or core samples to examine the physical characteristics and geochemistry of potential ore bodies and natural resource deposits. (STSE)

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss the engineering challenges (e.g., water incursion, sinkholes, Blairmore Formation for potash mining and ground support in hard rock mines), related to mining above and below ground in Saskatchewan. (STSE)

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine the moral and legal obligations of governments and companies involved in resource development with respect to traditional lands and treaties with First Nations, Métis and indigenous people worldwide. (STSE)

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Recognize the importance of water for various mining techniques such as solution mining and enhanced oil recovery. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Explain the operation of various surface and sub-surface resource extraction technologies and processes and their associated environmental impcts for mining and resources such as oil sands, shale oil and potash. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Research and investigate solutions to economic and environmental issues (e.g., managing mine tailings and pollutants, reclaiming open pit mining sites, ecological impact of pipelines, resource depletion and maintaining water quality) relatedto the extraction of geological resources in Saskatchewan(STSE)

outcomes.statement: Analyze surface geography as a product of deposition, weathering, erosion and mass wasting processes
outcomes.printedWith: SI, CP

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Observe, describe and locate common landforms (e.g., moraines, potholes, drumlins, buttes, coulees, dunes, oxbow lakes and river valleys) of Saskatchewan. (K)

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain how specific landforms are a consequence of depositional and denudation processes (e.g., weathering, erosion, and mass wasting). (K)

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain how surficial geological features of Saskatchewan such as the Athabasca Sand Dunes, Cypress Hills, Nipekamew Sand Cliffs and Qu'Appelle Valley are characterized by specific depositional and erosi onal processes. (K)

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the effects of mechanical weathering and erosion, including glaciation, on the surface geography of Saskatchewan as shown by landforms such as drumlins, moraines, eskers, kettles and outwash. (K)

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain the importance of chemical weathering to soil quality and formation, atmospheric carbon dioxide and geochemical cycling. (K, S)

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain how scientists use stratigraphic columns to infer sea level rise (transgression) and sea level fall (regression) over geologic time. (S, K)

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Speculate on the possible involvement of erosional processes in the development of geographic features found on Mars and other celestial bodies. (K, STSE, A)

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Design, construct and test a model of a structure or process to withstand or mitigate short term (e.g., flooding, wind storm, tsunami, storm surge and earthquake) or long term (e.g., erosion and sinkholes) phenomena that affect surface geography. (STSE, S)

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Apply mapping techniques such as creating and interpreting topographic profiles and translating between two-dimensional (2D) surface maps/cross-sections and three-dimensional (3D) box diagrams to represent surface geographical features. (K, S)

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Investigate how data gathered by technologies such as Earth orbiting satellites and drones can document changes in land forms and help to identify potential surface geological hazards. (K, STSE)

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Interpret and/or create a map of geological, civic and/or environmental data using a geographic information system (GIS) to correlate surface geography with human land use.(S, STSE)

outcomes.statement: Apply principles and techniques for injury prevention to ensure safety in the work area.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1A: General Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Recognize and apply safe and fair work practices including freedom from violence, harassment and bullying.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify industry standard personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety goggles, footwear, hearing protection, headwear and protective clothing.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Review the fire evacuation plan for the work area including the location of fire alarms, fire extinguishers and exits.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe ways to reduce personal injury or material and equipment damage as a result of unsafe work acts or environments.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss appropriate actions in case of an injury or accident, such as whom to contact and first-aid procedures.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of ventilation in a confined environment.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify hazardous materials and relevant WHMIS procedures.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe the importance of a clean work area and methods used to maintain a clean work area.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify risks and potential safety hazards (e.g., tools on floor, exposed live wires and extension cords).

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate safe practices when working with electricity and equipment.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2A: Electrical Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss risks and potential safety hazards common to the electrical industry.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify legislation and industry standards related to working with electricity and equipment.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the presence of live voltage using tools such as a multimeter or non-contact voltage tester.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate proper lockout and tagout procedures.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of ventilation in a confined environment when working with electrical devices such as a soldering iron.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices (e.g., check equipment for damaged wires and proper grounding and ensure work area is clean and dry) when working with electrical equipment.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Understand the need for circuit protection in electrical circuits.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Inspect electrical equipment for hazards before use.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Understand fall protection equipment (FPE) requirements and usage.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Discuss the uses of aerial work platforms (e.g., scissor lift) and fall protection.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when using elevation equipment (e.g., ladder, scissor lift and scaffolding).

outcomes.statement: Identify and use hand and power tools safely and appropriately.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3A: Hand and Power Tool Safety (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices associated with hand and power tools.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe safety precautions including the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) required for each tool used.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Select and use appropriate hand and power tools.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Classify tools according to their capabilities (e.g., cutting, striking and holding) and method of power (e.g., hand, power and electric).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Maintain and store tools appropriately.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Inspect tools before use, and in consultation with the instructor, tag out for repair as required.

outcomes.statement: Explain the purpose and structure of the Canadian Electrical Code (CEC).
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Canadian Electrical Code (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of electrical codes and regulations.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the organizational structure (e.g., sections, tables, diagrams and appendices) of the Canadian Electrical Code (CEC).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize that Canada and the United States have different electrical codes (i.e., Canadian Electrical Code and the National Electrical Code).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain SaskPower’s role related to electrical safety in Saskatchewan including the role of inspectors, electrical permits and interpretations of CEC rules.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Differentiate between jurisdiction specific simplified code books and the CEC.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Recognize that electrical information, whether online or print, may not be applicable in Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the relationship between building codes and electrical codes.

outcomes.statement: Explain the basics of electron theory.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5A: Electrical Principles - Electron Theory (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the structure of an atom, using Bohr’s atomic model, with respect to electrons, protons and neutrons.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the role of electrons as carriers of electric charge.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate that like charges repel and unlike charges attract (i.e., Law of Electrostatics).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Differentiate between static and current electricity.

outcomes.statement: Determine current, voltage and resistance in simple circuits.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5B: Electrical Principles - Current, Voltage and Resistance (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 5A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define common electrical terms including current, voltage, resistance, units of measurement (e.g., volts, amperes and ohms), insulators, semiconductors and conductors.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the relationship between current, voltage and resistance using Ohm’s Law (Voltage [V] = Current [I] x Resistance [R]).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Calculate current, voltage and resistance values for different simple circuits.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Verify the current, voltage and resistance readings in simple circuits.

outcomes.statement: Differentiate between alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC).
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5C: Electrical Principles - Alternating Current and Direct Current (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 5B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the operating principles of AC and DC.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the history of the competition between supporters of AC and DC.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify common applications of AC (e.g., house wiring and distribution of power) and DC (e.g., cell phones, flashlights and hybrid cars).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain why either AC or DC may be preferable for specific applications.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Draw common AC and DC waveforms.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Observe a sine wave and label the characteristic parts including cycle, wavelength, wave height, period and frequency.

outcomes.statement: Explore the concept of electromagnetism.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5D: Electrical Principles - Electromagnetism (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 5C

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe the characteristics of magnetic fields.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain how magnetic fields interact.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify characteristics of materials that act as insulators, materials that act as semiconductors and materials that act as conductors.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate the production of an electromagnetic field around a current carrying conductor.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: State the left-hand rule for current flow.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify factors (e.g., number of coils and amount of current) that influence electromagnetic field strength.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Construct and test a simple electromagnet.

outcomes.statement: Determine electric power in electric circuits.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5E: Electrical Principles - Electric Power (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 5D

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define electric power.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the relationship between power, voltage and current using Watt’s Law (Power [W] = Voltage [V] x Current [I]).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the relationship between the variables in Ohm’s Law and Watt’s Law.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Calculate power for different circuits using Watt’s Law.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Solve power output problems using Watt’s Law.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Calculate the electric power rating for equipment connected in series and parallel.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain how line loss affects voltage and power.

outcomes.statement: Explore electromagnetic induction.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5F: Electrical Principles - Inductance (Core) (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 5E

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the concept of electromagnetic induction.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate how a current can be induced by a magnetic field.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain how Faraday’s Law describes electromagnetic induction.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Provide examples of applications of electromagnetic induction such as transformers, induction motors and generators.

outcomes.statement: Explain how power is typically generated and distributed in Canada.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6A: Power Production and Distribution (Core) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Compare different types (e.g., coal, natural gas, hydro, solar, wind, nuclear, geothermal and biomass) of power generation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research how power is distributed (e.g., different voltage power lines, transformers, distribution substations and transformers) to residences, businesses and industry throughout Saskatchewan.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the transfer and conversion of electrical energy from a typical generating station to an end user.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Assess the efficiency of small scale versus large scale electrical energy distribution systems for homes and businesses.

outcomes.statement: Examine power production from renewable sources.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6B: Renewable Power Production and Distribution (Optional) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Compare the characteristics of various renewable power sources (e.g., residential photovoltaic solar, commercial solar and wind).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research different options (e.g., net metering, grid tie and off-grid battery storage and off-grid power sources) associated with renewable power generation.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain how power generated from renewable sources can be made available to the electrical grid, considering technologies such as DC solar, power inverters, grid tie devices, islanding devices and bi-directional meters.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze the economic benefits of generating power from renewable sources, considering factors such as payback period, technology costs and efficiency.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Design and/or construct a model of a power system that incorporates renewable sources.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Investigate the current and potential future status of power production from renewable sources in Saskatchewan.

outcomes.statement: Explore power production and distribution management systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6C: Power Production and Distribution Management (Optional) · Suggested Time: 4-6 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the historical development of electrical grids in North America, including the concept of smart grids.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe benefits (e.g., energy saving, lower energy rates, smooth and efficient functioning of the electric grid) associated with electrical grids.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss the advantages of the interconnection of electrical grids at various scales (e.g., individual facility, community, national and transnational).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare the features of traditional centralized electric grids with decentralized smart grids.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss how smart grid technologies (e.g., smart meters, sensors, remote monitoring equipment and distributed intelligent devices) enable utility companies and individual users to obtain real-time energy to inform energy-related decision making.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the potential impacts of smart grids on residential, commercial and industrial end users.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify challenges (e.g., cost, privacy and security) associated with implementing smart grids at various scales.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore the role of governments in providing incentives to reduce energy consumption and increase efficient functioning of the electrical grid.

outcomes.statement: Construct and analyze series and parallel electrical circuits.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7A: Simple Circuits - Series and Parallel (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-15 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 5C

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with electrical circuits.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the components of an electric circuit.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between a closed, open and short circuit.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the components of series and parallel circuits.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify whether a specific circuit is series or parallel.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Construct a simple series circuit that incorporates multiple loads.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Construct a simple parallel circuit that incorporates multiple loads.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Investigate the effects of changing the power source and number of loads within series and parallel circuits.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: State Kirchoff’s current and voltage laws.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain how Kirchhoff’s circuit laws relate to Ohm’s Law.

outcomes.statement: Construct and analyze combination electrical circuits.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7B: Simple Circuits - Combination (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 7A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with combination electrical circuits.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the purpose of combination circuits.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify series and parallel circuits within combination circuits.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Construct combination circuits that incorporate both series and parallel pathways.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Investigate potential effects of short circuits within combination circuits.

outcomes.statement: Design and construct a variety of electrical circuits.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Wiring Electrical Circuits (Core) · Suggested Time: 15-25 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 7B

indicators.label: a

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the advantages and disadvantages of different types (e.g., wall outlet, battery, solar and alternative) of power supplies for electronic applications.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Interpret datasheets to determine specifications (e.g., current, voltage, line regulation, load regulation, ripple and noise), features and applications of specific power supplies.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare different power supplies in terms of voltage, current, reliability and functionality.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the suitability of alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC) power supplies for electronic applications.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Justify a selected power supply for use in a specific electronic application.

outcomes.statement: Construct and test a rectifier for use in a power supply.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 31B: Power Supplies B (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 22B, 25A and 31A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with power supplies.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the purpose and operation of rectifiers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between half-wave, full-wave and bridge rectifiers.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Draw graphical representations of the output voltage of half-wave, full-wave and bridge rectifiers.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Construct and measure the output voltage of half-wave, full-wave and/or bridge rectifiers.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyze the shape of the output wave of half-wave, full-wave and bridge rectifiers using an oscilloscope.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Determine the most suitable type of rectifier for specific applications.

outcomes.statement: Explore the operating characteristics of power supplies.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 31C: Power Supplies C (Optional) · Suggested Time: 6-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 23A, 24B, 26C and 31A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate safe practices when working with power supplies.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the role of active and passive filters in power supplies.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain how capacitors are used in filter circuits in power supplies.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Diagram and explain the operation of a pi-filter configuration.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Troubleshoot defective filters.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain why ripple is undesirable in power supplies.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Express ripple in terms of percent.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Describe the action of the bleeder resistor in a power supply circuit.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Determine the value of a bleeder resistor.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Design a voltage regulator that incorporates a zener diode.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Explain the operation of a transistor regulated power supply.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Design a simple series feedback regulator using an operational amplifier (op-amp).

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Construct and test a power supply.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the role of inductance in tuned circuits.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 32A: Tuned Circuits and Oscillators A (Core) · Suggested Time: 15-20 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 5F, 7A, 22B, 23B and 24C

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain factors that affect inductance.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Determine the total inductance of inductors connected in series and of inductors connected in parallel.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain how inductive reactance is created in a circuit.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine the inductive reactance of a circuit.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compare the phase angle between voltage and current in an inductor.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Provide examples of applications of resistor-inductor (RL) circuits.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Construct and test RL circuits.

outcomes.statement: Examine the role of impedance, resonant frequency, bandwidth and oscillators in tuned circuits.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 32B: Tuned Circuits and Oscillators B (Optional) · Suggested Time: 15-20 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 32A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Compare impedance in alternating current circuits with resistance in direct current circuits.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Determine the impedance of circuits.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Determine the phase angle in series and parallel resistor-inductor-capacitor (RLC) circuits.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how series and parallel resonance occur in circuits.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Determine the resonant frequency of inductor-capacitor (LC) or RLC circuits.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Determine the value of the capacitor and the inductor required for resonance in LC circuits.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe factors affecting the Q and bandwidth of a resonant circuit.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Determine the bandwidth of resonant circuits.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Draw a typical resonance curve for both series and parallel resonant circuits.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Draw circuit diagrams and explain the operation of band-pass, band-stop, low-pass and high-pass filters.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Describe the conditions required for oscillation in circuits.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Identify LC oscillators in circuits.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Construct and analyze the effect of common (e.g., Hartley and Colpitts) LC oscillators on the resonant frequency of the circuit.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Construct and analyze the operation of a crystal oscillator circuit.

outcomes.statement: Compare the characteristics of amplitude modulation (AM) and frequency modulation (FM) methods of radio broadcasting.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research the development of AM and FM methods of radio broadcasting.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss the frequency ranges of AM and FM on the electromagnetic spectrum.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Compare the advantages and disadvantages of AM and FM broadcasting.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Compare how AM and FM waveforms are generated.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Draw a block diagram of an AM and an FM transmitter and describe the function of each component.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Draw a block diagram of an AM and an FM receiver and describe the function of each component.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Discuss the role of oscillators in AM and FM transmitters.

outcomes.statement: Examine the role of antennas in radio broadcasting.

indicators.text: Describe the function and operation of antennas in radio broadcasting.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss types of antennas used for transmission and reception of radio waves.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Draw the radiation pattern for a half-wave dipole antenna.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine the length of a half-wave dipole antenna for a specific wave length.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss factors, including skip, that affect the propagation of radio waves.

indicators.text: Describe the purpose of a logic gate in digital circuits.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Write a single truth table for a multi-input device.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Convert a Boolean expression to a logic gate circuit and a logic gate circuit to a Boolean expression.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Apply Demorgan’s theorem to Boolean expressions and logic gate circuits.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Design a logic gate circuit and verify the design by constructing a truth table.

indicators.text: Build and verify the operation of a logic gate circuit.

indicators.text: Provide examples of applications of sequential logic circuits.

indicators.text: Explain the operation of common flip-flop types, including SR, D, T and JK.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Construct and describe the operation of sequential logic circuits.

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80A: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III – Occupational Health and Safety in The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019:
- the right to know – the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate – in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse – work that you believe is unusually dangerous.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s performance during the interview.

- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?

- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?
