indicators.text: Assess the effects of pricing a product too high or pricing it too low.

indicators.label: i
j
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of offering a product in the right place and at the right time.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text:
Research considerations for product placement, such as:
- where potential customers are located;
- where and how potential customers shop (e.g., retail location and online); and,
- where the competition places their products.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Examine the role of promotion in gaining the attention of consumers and motivating them to take action (e.g., purchase a product or change behaviour).

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Identify paid (e.g., radio or television advertisements, print media and social advertisements) and free (e.g., organic social media and word of mouth) promotional opportunities.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Compare features of push and pull marketing.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Identify real-life examples of push and pull marketing.

indicators.label: p
q
indicators.text: Investigate advantages (e.g., global reach, cost efficiency and measurable results) and disadvantages (e.g., security and privacy issues, timeconsuming, and skills and training required) of online promotion.

indicators.label: r
indicators.text: Examine the application of the 4 Ps for a business, organization or brand/product of personal interest.

outcomes.statement: Investigate components of the extended marketing mix.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6B: The Extended Marketing Mix (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the three additional Ps (i.e., people, process and physical evidence) that have been added to the traditional marketing mix to create the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the reasons (e.g., easier to apply to services and the advent of online marketing and e-commerce) for the creation of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe various roles (e.g., salesperson, marketing team and customer service representative) that are considered part of the people element of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss desirable characteristics (e.g., effective and perceived positively by customers) associated with people roles in the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the role of brand voice in the people “P” of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Reflect on personal or observed positive and negative people experiences as a customer.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the process element of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research desirable characteristics (e.g., efficiency, reliability and sustainability) of effective processes in the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify examples (e.g., packaging, websites, and branding such as logos on employee uniforms and awards) associated with the physical evidence element of the extended marketing mix.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine the application of the extended marketing mix for a major global brand.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the use of digital and traditional marketing strategies.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Digital and Traditional Promotion (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between traditional (e.g., print, television, direct mail and outdoor advertising such as signage) and digital marketing (i.e., online).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify visible applications of traditional and digital marketing within the community.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Relate traditional and digital marketing to the promotion “P” in the marketing mix.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Assess advantages and disadvantages associated with traditional and digital marketing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine the relationship between user behaviour (i.e., of the target audience) to the selection and application of traditional and/or digital marketing strategies.

indicators.label: f
g
indicators.text: Assess the impact on marketing strategies of limitations (e.g., blocking of cookies) imposed by digital platforms.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Examine the use and impact of animation and video in modern marketing.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Defend the use of traditional, digital, or a hybrid of both types of marketing for a variety of given marketing scenarios.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify ways that consumer behaviour (e.g., online or through SMS) can be tracked and leveraged for marketing purposes.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Examine the types of consumer information that can be tracked through digital marketing.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Debate the ethics of tracking and leveraging consumer behaviour for marketing purposes.

indicators.label: m
indicators.text: Describe the concept of advertising avoidance.

indicators.label: n
indicators.text: Discuss actions (e.g., not sharing information, blocking pop-up advertisements on the computer and unsubscribing from newsletters) that consumers can take to avoid viewing or receiving advertising.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Propose ways in which marketers can effectively deal with consumer advertising avoidance.

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Investigate the origins, evolution and impact of influencer marketing to the present day.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into the process for becoming, and succeeding as, an influencer marketer.

indicators.label: r
indicators.text: Propose marketing strategies that may be effective to reach consumers of the future.

indicators.label: s
indicators.text: Develop a plan for promoting a business, brand or product of personal choice as an influencer marketer.

outcomes.statement: Assess the importance of market research for successful and effective marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Market Research (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 3

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the purpose and importance of ongoing market research for effective and successful marketing.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the correlation between market research and the ability to make sound business or operational decisions.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the importance of identifying and monitoring the competition as part of initial and ongoing market research.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Define qualitative and quantitative research.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe ways in which qualitative and quantitative research might be conducted and how the results might be used in marketing research.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Differentiate between primary and secondary market research.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify ways (e.g., observations and surveys such as pop-up or omnibus) in which primary data can be gathered.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the advantages (e.g., less costly than primary research and easier/quicker to gather) and disadvantages (e.g., datedness and reason for collecting may not align with one’s purposes) of secondary research.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text:
Identify sources of secondary data such as:
- government departments, libraries, business incubators and chambers of commerce (public and generally free);
- trade associations and research firms (commercial and generally associated with subscription or association fees); and,
- colleges, universities, technical institutes (academic).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Describe ways to confirm the credibility of sources of secondary data as well as the accuracy of that data.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Explain the concept of a target market.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Describe what market segmentation is and why it is beneficial.

indicators.label: m
n
indicators.text: Investigate how marketers use buyer personas to drive marketing success.

indicators.label: o
indicators.text: Outline the steps for creating a buyer persona.

indicators.label: p
indicators.text: Develop several buyer personas, including one for self.

indicators.label: q
indicators.text: Describe marketing strategies that would be effective with potential customers, including self, for a variety of products.

outcomes.statement: Assess the importance of ethical and socially responsible behaviour and marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9: Ethics and Social Responsibility (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 3

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Define ethics.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Describe good ethics in business as it relates to relationships between, but not limited to:
- businesses and customers;
- businesses and suppliers; and,
- employers and employees.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Assess the importance of regulations for both consumers and businesses.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Research the evolution and resulting impact of privacy and consumer protection laws on marketing practices in Saskatchewan and Canada.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe the importance of ethical behaviour and business ethics as they relate to ethical marketing.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify examples of types of false or misleading advertising such as bait and switch, price deception, unsubstantiated claims and misleading photos or illustrations.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Summarize the standards for marketing in Canada as detailed by the Canadian Marketing Association Code of Ethics and Standards.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Discuss the relationship among purpose-driven marketing, ethics and social responsibility.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Examine social responsibility and the benefits (e.g., to the business, consumer, society, the environment and others) of having a socially responsible marketing strategy.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Analyze the impact of marketing strategies used by local, provincial (e.g., tentree), national (e.g., Manitobah Mukluks) and international (e.g., The Body Shop, Toms, and Proctor and Gamble—Dawn Soap) companies that promote themselves as being socially responsible.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Research ways (e.g., Certified B Corporations) to verify a company’s claim of being socially responsible.

outcomes.statement: Examine the importance of inclusive marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Inclusive Marketing (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 4, 9

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe inclusive marketing.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain accessible marketing as a component of inclusive marketing.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research ways that marketing content can be more easily accessed by users of all abilities (e.g., audio or larger text for individuals with vision impairments, print for individuals with hearing impairments and digital content for individuals with motor impairments) or by users with limited access (e.g., print materials or television content for individuals with no or limited access to the Internet).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the impact that inclusive marketing can have on a brand (e.g., creating loyalty and trust) and on others (e.g., giving voice to a marginalized group).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of cultural understanding in developing effective and culturally sensitive marketing content.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Differentiate between cultural appropriation and cultural appreciation.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine the potential impact of using cultural appropriation and cultural appreciation in marketing campaigns.

indicators.label: h
i
indicators.text: Explain, and provide examples of, stereotype marketing.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Justify stereotype marketing as an exclusive, rather than inclusive, marketing strategy.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Brainstorm examples (e.g., a dad making dinner or a mom fixing a lawn mower) of marketing that challenge stereotypes.

outcomes.statement: Examine the relationship between marketing and customer experiences.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Customer Experience Marketing (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 2

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Differentiate between customer service and customer experiences.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain what customer-centric marketing means and the importance of a business or organization knowing and understanding its customers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the benefits (e.g., greater brand loyalty and improved customer retention) of such marketing efforts.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of monitoring, managing and responding to online and other reviews.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Propose strategies for replying to both positive and negative online reviews.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify the stages (e.g., pre-purchase, purchase and post-purchase) of a customer journey map.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore effective marketing strategies for connecting with consumers at each of the stages.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Reflect on personal encounters with poor and exemplary customer experiences.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Describe characteristics of ideal customer experiences.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Assess the role that marketers play in creating and supporting the ideal customer experience through customer experience marketing.

outcomes.statement: Investigate careers in marketing.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Careers in Marketing (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 1, 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research opportunities and trends in marketing careers in Saskatchewan, Canada and the world.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare the marketing services offered by a variety of Saskatchewan-based marketing or advertising companies.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the roles, responsibilities, educational qualifications and personal and professional qualities typically required by those who work in marketing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text:
Generate a list of questions to ask a professional in the marketing industry to learn about their work; questions may include:
- What do you do?
- What knowledge and skills do you use every day?
- What does a typical day look like for you?
- What is the most interesting marketing project you have worked on?

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: List personal interests, skills, abilities and traits that may lead to a career in marketing.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research which marketing occupations are facing shortages and which are oversubscribed locally, regionally and/or provincially.

indicators.label: g
h

outcomes.statement: Examine the benefits of a positive health and safety culture in the marketing workplace.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13: Health and Safety in the Marketing Workplace (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 12

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Discuss the impact of a workplace injury on the injured and others including the employer, work colleagues, family and friends.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Describe the importance and benefits of a positive health and safety culture at work.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Define a workplace hazard.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify potential physical hazards (e.g., exposure to allergens such as perfumes and other scents, sitting for long periods of time and eye strain) associated with office work.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Research causes of stress and anxiety (e.g., little or no results from a marketing campaign and time pressures) for those working in marketing careers.

indicators.label: g
h
i
indicators.text: Compare the hazards associated with working remotely to working in an office environment.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Explain why some brands align themselves with safety messaging such as Mission Zero.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Develop a marketing campaign that promotes a positive health and safety culture in the marketing workplace.

indicators.label: l
indicators.text: Reflect on personal and collective responsibility for, and commitment to, developing and supporting a positive health and safety culture at work.

outcomes.statement: Examine characteristics and components of a strategic marketing plan.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14A: Strategic Marketing Plan A (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 6A or 6B, 7, 8, 9

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain a value proposition.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify examples of value propositions presented by several brands.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the relationship between a value proposition and strategic marketing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Discuss the importance and interrelatedness of the marketing mix (i.e., traditional or extended) for strategic marketing.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Research tenets of an effective marketing campaign such as consistency (e.g., of message, brand, tone and relevancy), frequency (e.g., of message; less effective advertisements require more frequency) and creativity (e.g., amusing; engaging; and featuring well-designed imagery, video or text).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the purpose of a marketing plan.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Assess characteristics (e.g., organized, easy to read, clear section headings and free of grammar or spelling errors) of prepared strategic marketing plans.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Analyze the impact of finances on a marketing plan.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text:
Describe the elements of prepared marketing plans, such as:
- market analysis (e.g., purpose and mission of the business or organization; description of current markets and strategies; primary competitors; and SWOT [i.e., strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats] analysis);
- marketing strategy (e.g., goals and expected outcomes, target market description, marketing mix); and,
- implementation (e.g., activity schedule including responsibilities, schedule and budget; evaluation procedures including evidence of success and methods of collecting the evidence).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Identify reasons for changing or recalibrating a marketing plan.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Develop a commercial or social marketing plan with a budgetary limit.

outcomes.statement: Develop, implement, manage and evaluate the success of a marketing campaign.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14B: Strategic Marketing Plan B (Optional) · Suggested Time: 15-20 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 14A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research companies and organizations (e.g., local businesses, not-forprofits and school or community clubs and teams) as potential clients or beneficiaries for a marketing campaign.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Assess the pros and cons of the various companies and organizations researched to determine the best option(s) for a project.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Analyze marketing strategies used by companies and organizations that are considered competitors.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Collaborate with the chosen company or organization to develop a marketing plan.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Implement the marketing plan.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Monitor the implementation of the marketing plan and make adjustments, as required, throughout the process.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Conclude and evaluate the success of the marketing campaign based upon the criteria outlined in the marketing plan.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Reflect on personal contributions to, and personal growth resulting from, developing, implementing, managing and evaluating the marketing campaign.

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Describe and reflect on the three basic rights that all workers have under Part III – Occupational Health and Safety in The Saskatchewan Employment Act, 2019:
- the right to know – the hazards at work and how to control them;
- the right to participate – in finding and controlling workplace hazards; and,
- the right to refuse – work that you believe is unusually dangerous.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: e
f
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?
- Where do I find fire extinguishers, first aid kits and emergency assistance?
- What type of safety gear am I expected to wear? Is it provided?
- What should I do if I get injured or have an accident in the workplace?
- How can I contact my health and safety committee or representative?
- Are there any health and safety procedures I should follow?
- Who is the first aid person?
- Where are safety notices posted?
- What should I do in case of a fire or emergency?

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop a list of questions that could potentially be asked by the employer/work placement in an interview situation as well as answers to the questions.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Participate in an interview with the employer prior to beginning the work placement.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Reflect upon one’s performance during the interview.

outcomes.statement: Participate in a work placement experience.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 81: Work Study Placement (Optional) · Suggested Time: 25-50 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 80

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply relevant skills and abilities during the work placement experience.

indicators.label: b
c
indicators.text: Document knowledge and awareness of employment standards, safety, workplace ethics, rights and responsibilities, occupational health and safety, and networking observed during the work placement.

outcomes.statement: Relate one’s work placement experience to personal and career goals.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 82: Work Study Follow-up (Optional) · Suggested Time: 2-4 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 81

indicators.label: a
b
indicators.text: Reflect on the attainment of personal and learning goals.

indicators.text: Update personal career documentation (e.g., resume, portfolio) following the work placement.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Prepare a letter, note, card or other communication for the work placement employer, expressing appreciation.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Develop and/or revise personal and career goals based on the work placement experience.

outcomes.statement: Develop an awareness of the automotive industry.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Automotive Industry (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explore the history of the automobile and automotive industry.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify and explain the operation of an automobile’s major systems (e.g., steering, suspension, brakes, drive train, cooling, lubrication, engine).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe processes used to identify automotive system faults.

indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices when performing automotive diagnosis and repair, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe common practices and procedures involved in automotive repair.

indicators.text: Identify steps (e.g., identify, diagnose, repair and confirm the repair) common to automotive diagnostic processes.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Use appropriate service information to identify proper repair processes for a specific problem.

indicators.text: Identify required components, and compile a parts list and cost estimate, for a specific repair or modification process.

indicators.label: g

indicators.text: Identify, label, store and handle hazardous materials according to Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS 2015).

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Recognize and apply safe and fair work practices, including freedom from violence, harassment and bullying.

outcomes.statement: Apply principles and techniques for injury prevention to ensure safety in the automotive workplace.

indicators.text: Identify the importance of safety when undertaking automotive service procedures, including safety hazards and preventative measures common to the automotive industry.

indicators.label: b

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Inspect and utilize protective devices on equipment.

indicators.label: d

indicators.label: e

indicators.label: f

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Describe the importance of a clean workplace and methods used to maintain a clean workplace.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Locate, identify and explain the correct use of safety equipment (e.g., eye wash station and first aid station) in the workplace.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate safe procedures to lift and support vehicles.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Vehicle Lifting and Support (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow appropriate safe practices related to lifting and supporting vehicles, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify appropriate lifting and support equipment needed for the task.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify lift and balance points for different types of vehicles.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Position vehicles safely and correctly before lifting.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Lift and lower vehicles in a safe manner using floor jacks and jack stands.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Raise large drivetrain assemblies using hoists and transmission jacks.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Lift and lower vehicles on a hoist in a safe manner using proper procedures.

outcomes.statement: Explore factors to consider related to vehicle purchase.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Vehicle Purchase (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Prepare a budget prior to purchasing a vehicle.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between personal wants and needs based on a specific budget.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss factors (e.g., environmental impact of a vehicle, the cost of operations and potential repair costs) to consider when purchasing a vehicle.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify vehicles that fit criteria based on personal budget, wants and needs.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Analyze potential vehicles for purchase based on customer, commercial and technical reviews.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain and/or perform procedures for inspecting and testing vehicles before purchase.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify safety practices to follow when inspecting and testing vehicles.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Estimate potential repair costs of any service or repair needed for a used vehicle.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain insurance, financing and warranty options for purchasing or leasing a new or used vehicle.

outcomes.statement: Locate automotive service information utilizing appropriate sources.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6: Automotive Service Information (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the type of information available from common automotive service information sources (e.g., manuals, computers, scan tools, diagnostic charts, technical bulletins and apps).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Determine correct service information such as torque specifications, wiring diagrams and disassembly/assembly procedures from appropriate sources.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate care in handling manuals, computers and scan tools.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyze vehicle identification numbers (VIN) and compliance labels.

outcomes.statement: Use and maintain hand and power tools and equipment following safe procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Hand and Power Tools (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices when working with hand and power tools, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Classify tools according to their capabilities (e.g., cutting, striking and holding) and method of power (e.g., hand, power, electric and hydraulic).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Maintain and store tools and equipment appropriately.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Recognize that metric and imperial systems of measurement are both used in the automotive industry.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify, select and use appropriate tools for specific tasks.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Inspect tools before use and tag for repair as required.

outcomes.statement: Identify, select and use automotive fasteners properly.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Automotive Fasteners (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices when working with automotive fasteners, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe common categories (e.g., clips, pins, nuts, bolts, washers, screws and rivets) of automotive fasteners.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify fasteners based on specifications such as metric/SAE, grade, length, diameter and thread pitch.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe types (e.g., hex, 12 point and Torx) of fastener heads commonly found in automotive applications.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify and use appropriate tools to manipulate fasteners.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Discuss the importance of torqueing fasteners, including following a fastener tightening sequence.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Determine torque values and sequences for specific fasteners.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Adjust and use torque wrenches and/or angle gauges to properly tighten fasteners.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Perform fastener related tasks such as extraction, thread repair and tap and die selection and use.

outcomes.statement: Explain the characteristics of automotive lubricants.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9A: Automotive Lubricants (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the functions and properties of automotive fluids and lubricants.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between synthetic and non-synthetic lubricants.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between different oil service ratings (e.g., SAE viscosity grades, API service ratings and original equipment manufacturer [OEM] specifications).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the function of various oil additives.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain ways in which oil can be contaminated and the potential effects of contaminated oil on an engine.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain safe and sustainable procedures for disposal of automotive fluids, containers and components.

outcomes.statement: Maintain outdoor power and recreation equipment following appropriate procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9B: Outdoor Power and Recreation Equipment Maintenance (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices when working with outdoor power and recreation equipment, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify components of outdoor power and recreation equipment that require periodic lubrication.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Perform general maintenance (e.g., check belt tension, inspect spark plug and perform winterization procedures) on outdoor power and recreation equipment and accessories such as blades, augers and tines.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Inspect and evaluate the condition of drive mechanisms (e.g., chains, belts, pulleys and continuously variable transmissions [CVTs]) on outdoor power and recreation equipment.

outcomes.statement: Explain basic automotive maintenance procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9C: Introductory Automotive Maintenance (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify appropriate safety procedures related to automotive maintenance.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain common procedures for periodic inspection and testing of automobiles.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain common procedures to perform automotive maintenance based on manufacturers' specifications.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify and inspect basic components (e.g., tires, fluid levels, wipers, lights) of an automobile that require periodic inspection and/or lubrication.

outcomes.statement: Perform appropriate automotive maintenance procedures safely and correctly.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9D: Automotive Maintenance (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices when performing automotive maintenance procedures, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Locate and follow manufacturer’s lubrication and maintenance schedules.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify and choose lubricant types and filters for different vehicles and service conditions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Perform automotive drivetrain (e.g., engine, transmission, transfer case, differential) lubricant and filter changes.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Perform manufacturer recommended system maintenance such as checking spark plugs, fuel filters and positive crankcase ventilation valves.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Perform chassis and body lubrication according to manufacturers’ specifications.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Perform complete multi-point vehicle inspections (e.g., belts, hoses, leaks, constant velocity [CV] boots).

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive tires and wheels.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Automotive Tires and Wheels (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., follow proper inflation procedures to avoid explosive hazards and be aware of cut and pinch points) when working with automotive tires and wheels, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain how tire condition affects vehicle handling, fuel economy and safety characteristics.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the design and construction of tires and wheels, including tire sidewall information.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Choose the correct tire size and type according to manufacturer’s recommendations for specific vehicle and performance applications.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the consequences of installing tires of inappropriate sizes.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Evaluate tire condition (e.g., tread depth, wear patterns and rubber condition) and explain causes and effects of tire damage, wear and defects.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain when and why tire service, such as tire rotation and balancing, is required.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Perform tire and wheel related service operations such as rotation, dismounting and mounting, balancing and repair.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Explain tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) repair, relearn and programming procedures.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Follow correct torqueing procedures for all tires and wheels and discuss how improper torqueing can be a safety issue.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive wheel bearings and hubs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11: Automotive Wheel Bearings (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., avoid dry spinning bearings with air and follow correct procedures when working with bearing presses) when working with automotive wheel bearings, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify common automotive bearing types.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Handle, clean and repack wheel bearings following appropriate procedures.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Inspect and evaluate wheel bearings and hub condition.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Remove and install wheel bearings, cups and seals using appropriate tools and equipment.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Remove and install wheel bearing hub assemblies.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Adjust wheel bearing pre-load appropriately.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Follow correct torqueing procedures for all wheel bearing fasteners and discuss how improper torqueing can be a safety issue.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive hydraulic systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12: Automotive Hydraulics (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., avoid having pressurized hydraulic fluids pierce the skin or enter the bloodstream and avoid contact with brake fluid on painted surfaces) when working with automotive hydraulic systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate the proper procedures for disposal of used hydraulic fluids and explain potential environmental concerns associated with disposal of hydraulic fluids.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the properties of different hydraulic fluids (e.g., brake fluid and power steering fluid).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how Pascal’s law applies to force, pressure and area in hydraulic systems.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Diagnose common hydraulic system failures such as air and fluid leaks.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Diagnose and repair hydraulic failures in automotive hydraulic systems (e.g., brake, clutch and power steering).

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive brake systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13A: Automotive Brake Systems (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Modules 12

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of asbestos dust from brake components, avoid dust inhalation and avoid contact with brake fluid on painted surfaces) when working with automotive brake systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: List the properties, maintenance and testing procedures of different types of automotive brake fluids.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the construction, application, and inspection of brake components (e.g., brake hoses, lines, wheel cylinders, calipers, drums, rotors and hardware).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain how principles of friction apply to disc and drum brake systems.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss factors that influence automotive brake performance.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the purpose, construction and operation of electric, hydraulic and vacuum power brake assist systems.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Identify common brake problems and related diagnostic procedures.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Perform common automotive brake system scheduled maintenance such as resurfacing brake drums and disc rotors.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Remove, install and/or adjust brake system components and bleed air from hydraulic brake systems using appropriate methods and tools.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Follow correct torqueing procedures for all brake systems fasteners and discuss how improper torqueing can be a safety issue.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair anti-lock brake systems (ABS).
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13B: Antilock Brake Systems (ABS) (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 13A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of residual pressures and ensure all electrical wiring is located away from moving parts) when working with antilock brake systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify the different types of ABS and their use in braking, stability control and traction control.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the function and operation of ABS and their components.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Diagnose and perform ABS repairs according to manufacturers' recommended procedures, including bleeding the system as necessary.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Follow correct torqueing procedures for all ABS fasteners and discuss how improper torqueing can be a safety issue.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive suspension systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14A: Automotive Suspension Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of the dangers of welding or heating steering linkage components and be aware of spring tension) when working with automotive suspension systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe how different types of springs (e.g., leaf, coil, torsion bar and air) are used in automotive suspension systems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the operation of suspension components (e.g., shocks, struts, sway bars and ball joints) and their effects on vehicle stability.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Inspect and evaluate suspension component condition for damage, corrosion, wear and excessive play.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Diagnose and perform repair procedures (e.g., remove and replace parts in pairs, disassemble and reassemble a strut and spring assembly and replace ball joints) on automotive suspension systems using appropriate equipment (e.g., ball joint press and strut spring compressor).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Make preliminary wheel alignment adjustments after suspension components (e.g., struts and control arms) have been replaced.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Follow correct torqueing procedures for all suspensions systems fasteners and discuss how improper torqueing can be a safety issue.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive steering systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14B: Automotive Steering Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of the dangers of welding or heating steering linkage components) when working with automotive steering systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare the operation and components of linkage and rack-and-pinion steering systems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the parameters (e.g., caster, camber and toe) that affect wheel alignment and how misalignment of each can affect vehicle handling and tire wear.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe how steering component wear or damage can affect handling, steering control and alignment geometry.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Inspect and assess steering components for damage, corrosion, wear and excessive play.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Diagnose and perform common steering system repairs using appropriate equipment.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Make preliminary wheel alignment adjustments after replacing steering components (e.g., pitman or idler arm and tie rods).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Follow correct torqueing procedures for all steering systems fasteners and discuss how improper torqueing can be a safety issue.

outcomes.statement: Measure and adjust wheel alignments.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14C: Wheel Alignments (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 14B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., ensure proper connection of wheel alignment equipment and be aware of pinch points) when performing wheel alignments including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Connect wheel alignment equipment appropriately to obtain alignment data.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Read and interpret wheel alignment data to determine which adjustments are necessary.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Make final wheel alignment adjustments according to manufacturer’s specifications, measured with an alignment machine.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive cooling systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15: Automotive Cooling Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., check coolant pressure and temperature) when working with automotive cooling systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate the proper procedures for disposal of used coolants and explain potential environmental concerns associated with antifreeze disposal.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe how cooling systems remove and dissipate heat from engines, including the role of antifreeze.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the function of the components of a liquid cooling system.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compare the operation of liquid and air cooling systems.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Perform common cooling system tests (e.g., visual inspection, pressure tests, leak detection and coolant tests) and maintenance procedures (e.g., checking fluid levels and flushing the cooling system).

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Diagnose and perform common automotive cooling system repairs such as removing and replacing belts, radiator, water pump and thermostat.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Fill automotive coolant systems according to specifications and purge air from systems where required.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive heating and ventilation systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16A: Automotive Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) Systems A (Optional) · Suggested Time: 8-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 15

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., check coolant pressure and temperature, be aware of moving components and pressurized refrigerants) when working with automotive HVAC systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate the proper procedures for disposal of used coolants.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain potential environmental concerns associated with improper coolant disposal.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe the function and operation of HVAC systems to heat, vent and cool passenger compartment.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Perform common HVAC system tests (e.g., visual inspection, pressure tests, leak detection and coolant tests) and maintenance procedures (e.g., checking fluid levels and flushing the heater core).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Diagnose and perform common HVAC system repairs such as repairing system leaks, replacing heater cores, blower motors, fuses and fan belts and cleaning evaporators, condensers and heater cores.

outcomes.statement: Examine the procedures required to diagnose, service and repair automotive air conditioning systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16B: Automotive Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) Systems B (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Modules 16A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., check coolant pressure and temperature, be aware of moving components and pressurized refrigerants) when working with automotive air conditioning systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the proper procedures for collection, storage and recycling of refrigerants.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain potential environmental concerns associated with improper refrigerant collection.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine regulations and legislation related to automotive air conditioning systems.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Describe how to perform common air conditioning system tests (e.g., visual inspection, pressure tests and leak detection) and maintenance procedures (e.g., recharging the system).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe the procedures for common air conditioning system repairs such as repairing refrigerant leaks and replacing fan belts, fuses, air conditioning compressor, condenser or radiator.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive exhaust systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17: Automotive Exhaust Systems (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of hot surfaces and dangers of using pipe bending equipment) when working with automotive exhaust systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Dispose of automotive exhaust system components such as catalytic converters properly.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the function and operation of automotive exhaust systems and their components.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Apply appropriate care and attention when working with fragile exhaust components such as O2 sensors, catalytic converters and ceramics.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Inspect and evaluate exhaust systems for leaks, mounting issues, corrosion, blockage and noise.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Diagnose and repair common automotive exhaust system faults.

outcomes.statement: Investigate the operation and repair of small engines.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 18: Small Engines (Core) · Suggested Time: 30-40 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of pinch points, hot surfaces, sharp surfaces and moving parts) when working with small engines, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the operating principles of an internal combustion engine.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between 2-stroke and 4-stroke engine operation.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the construction and function of major engine sub-assemblies, including the cylinder block, head, and valve train.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate how repair manuals can guide engine disassembly, repair, and reassembly.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the relationship and operation of major engine components.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Define and determine engine measurements, such as clearance, out of round and taper.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explain how improper lubrication or cooling can contribute to engine failure.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Identify types of specialized measuring equipment and use appropriate procedures to measure and evaluate engine condition.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Disassemble and reassemble an operational small engine.

indicators.label: k
indicators.text: Use appropriate procedures to start, run and stop a small engine.

outcomes.statement: Explain multi-cylinder engine construction and operation.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 19A: Multi-cylinder Engine Theory (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 18

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the construction and function of major engine sub-assemblies (e.g., cooling, exhaust, lubrication systems) in multi-cylinder engines.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Differentiate between common automotive engine configurations (e.g., inline, V-type and opposed).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between common automotive valve train configurations (e.g., cam in block, single overhead camshaft and dual overhead camshaft) in multi-cylinder engines.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe how the events of combustion change with different fuel sources (e.g., diesel, varying octane gasoline and compressed natural gas [CNG]).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Compare the air flow of naturally aspirated and forced air (e.g., supercharged and turbocharged) engines.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explain the purpose and operation of internal engine components (e.g., camshaft, crankshaft and pistons) and variations (e.g., cam lift, piston shape and ring design) of each component.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Define and determine engine measurements such as displacement, compression ratio and clearance.

outcomes.statement: Perform basic engine diagnosis, testing and repair.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 19B: Engine Testing, Diagnosis and Repair (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 19A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of high voltage shock hazards, pinch points, hot surfaces, sharp surfaces, moving parts and fire hazards) when performing basic engine diagnosis, testing and repair, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Follow established systematic diagnosis procedures, including visual inspections and diagnostic tests, to identify specific engine problems.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Adjust, repair and/or replace engine components to solve problems and optimize performance.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore how engine modifications can affect engine performance.

outcomes.statement: Overhaul multicylinder engines safely and following correct procedures.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 19C: Multi-cylinder Engine Overhaul (Optional) · Suggested Time: 40-60 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 19A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of pinch points, hot surfaces, sharp surfaces, moving parts, cleaning agents and fire hazards) when working with multi-cylinder engines, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss typical steps involved in overhauling multi-cylinder engines.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Follow appropriate procedures to disassemble and reassemble multicylinder engines.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify types of specialized measuring equipment and use appropriate procedures to measure and evaluate engine condition (e.g., clearance, taper and out of round).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Remove and replace gaskets, seals and O-rings.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Inspect and clean engine internal systems.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Tighten fasteners using correct specifications and sequences.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Verify that all components are properly installed and configured.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Perform proper engine start-up and run-in procedures.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair drive shafts and universal joints.

indicators.label: a

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the purpose, function and common configurations of automotive drivelines.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the construction and operation of driveline components such as universal joints, constant velocity (CV) joints and drive shafts.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify and inspect drivelines for common causes of failure such as vibration, incorrect running angle and play.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify repair options for common driveline failures.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Perform common repairs on driveline components such as universal joints, CV shaft/boot and center bearing.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair clutches and release mechanisms.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of asbestos dust from clutch components, avoid dust inhalation, avoid having pressurized hydraulic fluids pierce the skin or enter the bloodstream and be aware of component weight) when working with clutches and release mechanisms, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explain the purpose and function of clutch assemblies.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Describe the construction and operation of clutch assemblies, including clutch fork and release bearing mechanisms.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the implications of slippage and excessive free play in a clutch.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify common symptoms and faults associated with clutches.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Perform common clutch and release mechanism scheduled maintenance such as adjusting cables and linkages.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Diagnose and perform clutch and release mechanism repairs (e.g., clutch disc, pressure plate, flywheel, release mechanism, adjustments and alignment).

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair manual transmissions and transaxles.

indicators.text: Demonstrate the proper procedures for disposal of used transmission oil and explain potential environmental concerns associated with disposal of transmission oil.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the purpose and function of manual transmissions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explain the construction and operation of manual transmission gearing, including synchromesh.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Calculate gear ratios and identify power flow through manual transmissions for all forward and reverse gears.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify common symptoms and faults associated with manual transmissions.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Diagnose and perform manual transmission repairs (e.g., remove and replace transmission/transaxle, inspect and clear transmission vents and change oil).

indicators.label: a

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate proper procedures for disposal of used transmission oil and explain potential environmental concerns associated with disposal of transmission oil.

indicators.label: f

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe the function and operation of transfer cases.

indicators.label: c

indicators.label: d

indicators.label: c

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive storage batteries.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., be aware of battery acid, overheating and gas emissions) when working with automotive storage batteries, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Follow appropriate procedures for disposing of automotive storage batteries.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain the construction and operation of common types (e.g., lead acid, gel cell, absorbent glass mat [AGM]) of automotive storage batteries.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify battery ratings, such as cold cranking amperes (CCA) and reserve capacity minutes.

indicators.label: e

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Follow appropriate connection order when performing battery replacement, charging and boosting operations.

indicators.label: g

outcomes.statement: Explore the function and operation of automotive electrical systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 27A: Fundamentals of Automotive Electricity and Electronics (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., grounding static electricity, being aware of high voltage electric drives, avoiding lead solder fumes and connecting batteries correctly) when working with automotive electrical systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Describe major electrical concepts, including atomic structure, insulators, conductors and semi-conductors.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Differentiate between voltage, resistance, current and their units of measurement.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify factors (e.g., length, diameter, material, temperature, connection quality and corrosion) that affect resistance and their effect on current and voltage.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify various sources of voltage (e.g., electro-chemical, thermal electric, piezo electric and photo electric) in automotive settings.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Apply Ohm’s law and the power equation to electrical circuits.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Differentiate between the characteristics of series, parallel and seriesparallel electric circuits.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Diagnose and perform electrical repairs by splicing, soldering, taping and/or using heat shrink tubing.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Assess the quality of electrical repairs.

outcomes.statement: Diagnose, service and repair automotive electrical systems.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 27B: Advanced Automotive Electricity and Electronics (Optional) · Suggested Time: 15-30 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 27A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., grounding static electricity, being aware of high voltage electric drives, avoiding lead solder fumes and connecting batteries correctly) when working with automotive electrical systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify common electrical and electronic components in automotive circuits.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify and select appropriate wire gauge, connectors and circuit protection devices (e.g., fuses and breakers).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Interpret electrical system wiring diagrams (e.g., lighting, horns, windows and doors) to help diagnose electrical problems.

indicators.label: e

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Provide examples of common faults (e.g., short to ground, short circuit, high resistance, open circuit and mechanical resistance) that may occur in automotive electrical circuits.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Diagnose and repair common automotive electrical faults using appropriate diagnostic techniques.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Perform mechanical adjustments (e.g., headlight, camera, sensor and switch alignments) to automotive electrical system components.

indicators.text: Identify and follow safe work practices (e.g., disconnect battery and prevent grounding of live wires) when working with automotive charging systems, including maintaining a clean and organized work area.

outcomes.statement: Prepare for the work placement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 80A: Work Study Preparation (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate, Advanced · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the roles and responsibilities of each partner (e.g., student, parent, teacher or other school staff, employer) involved in the work placement.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Research the business/organization to become familiar with its operations.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: In collaboration with all partners, develop personal and learning goals for the work placement.

indicators.label: d
e
indicators.text: Compile an employer information package that includes documents needed for the work placement (e.g., personal career documentation such as a resume or portfolio, permission forms, logs, self- and employer evaluation forms).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text:
Brainstorm a list of questions to ask the employer before beginning the work placement; these may include:
- What is my schedule of work hours?
- Who is my supervisor?
- What should I wear?
- When will I be provided with safety training?
- What potential hazards might I encounter in the work placement?

indicators.label: d

indicators.label: b

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: seeks information to further understanding of Michif concepts from Elders and other knowledge keepers within the community;

indicators.label: d

indicators.label: j

indicators.label: k

outcomes.statement: understand and interpret language as a connected set of ideas expressed in sentences.

indicators.label: a

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: interprets and explains or invites a speaker to share traditional narratives of the people: histories, moral stories, songs, informational texts, inspirational speeches;

indicators.label: c

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: interprets contemporary reflections in various mediums that relate to cultural areas of study, such as documentaries on social problems in the community, theatre, magazine articles;

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: reads and interprets text that has been transcribed from the oral tradition of Michif people on a topic that is familiar to the student (contemporary lifestyles, fishing, hunting);

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: reads and interprets informational text that may be unfamiliar but relevant to research needs of the student; and,

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: translates text between a Michif language and another language.

outcomes.statement: produce language that is understandable to others.

indicators.label: a

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: shares personal reflections created such as a speech or a written text, in response to personal experiences or areas of cultural study;

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: researches and reports historical information relating to current issues, such as residential schooling as it relates to present problems;

indicators.label: d

indicators.label: e

outcomes.statement: select and use appropriate strategies to maximize learning and communication.

indicators.label: a

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: seeks information through a network of sources (e.g., libraries, internet, others, agencies);

indicators.label: c

outcomes.statement: communicate meaningfully with accuracy (accuracy is primarily the grammatical system of a language).

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: creates a variety of basic sentences using accurate grammar;

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: uses complex sentences and phrases but not without error;

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: uses idioms, and basic and specialized vocabulary from course content, to communicate ideas;

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: uses understanding of the varying sound systems of different dialects to understand them better; and,

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: reads factual texts or concrete information from a cultural study or prose that is relatively straight forward.

outcomes.statement: communicate meaningfully with proficiency (proficiency involves the ease with which communication is expressed or received).

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: produces several sentences of spoken, coherent discourse, with relative detail and precision, in spontaneous situations;

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: produces a variety of lengthy texts on topics, providing details to support the main point;

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: communicates thoughts, ideas, and feelings for specific purposes and audiences through a variety of verbal and visual media;

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: listens to and reiterates what another speaker has said, though the listener may need passage repeated or explained; and,

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: sustains conversations for up to 15 minutes.

outcomes.statement: communicate meaningfully with coherency (coherency relates to the connectedness of information, thoughts and ideas within communication)

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: uses complex and compound sentences to hold ideas in discourse together;

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: uses linking devices throughout the discourse, though not with complete agreement;

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: uses sentences and questions that contain learned vocabulary and familiar language structures in different forms;

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: adjusts language to suit audience and purpose;

indicators.label: e
