outcomes.statement: Investigate techniques (i.e., instrumental, vocal or creative technologies) and the elements of music for solo and/or ensemble performances.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate instrumental or vocal technique and knowledge of the elements of music.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Develop vocabulary appropriate to genre or musical context.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: With guidance, generate technique-related inquiry questions and set short term goals for personal improvement based on the inquiry findings.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Develop the skills and techniques required for successful ensemble performances.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate knowledge of one’s own role within an ensemble.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Track development of instrumental or vocal techniques and develop strategies to improve.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Develop the ability to communicate and interact with ensemble members and/or audience.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Demonstrate musicality (e.g., emotional expressiveness) in solo and/or ensemble performance.

outcomes.statement: Experiment with various types of notation to communicate musical ideas (e.g., graphic/invented, tablature, standard and culture-specific forms).

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Read and interpret written musical communication.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate legal and ethical practices in music composition, performance and recording.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Represent musical ideas using standard notation (i.e., Western music notation, tablature).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Represent musical ideas using non-standard notation (e.g., abstract symbols and text, time-based pictographs, rap and hip hop flow diagrams with lyrics under beat numbers, braille, colour coded) and/or culture specific forms and models (e.g., unwritten, memorized with fixed and/or variable elements).

outcomes.statement: Compose to express musical ideas experimenting with the elements of music and principles of composition, respecting cultural contexts.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Express musical ideas, through composition individually and/or in ensemble settings, that can be recreated by others.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Understand and experiment with the elements of music (i.e., melody, harmony, rhythm, dynamics, form, tone, texture) and principles of composition (e.g., repetition and variation, tension and resolution, balance and unity).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate, through rehearsal, an ability to reflect on, refine and revise solo and ensemble compositions.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Apply aural skills to making musical decisions for sound compositions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Discuss the difference between ‘drawing inspiration from music’ versus ‘engaging in cultural appropriation or copyright infringement’ when composing.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine music composition processes within diverse genres and cultural contexts (e.g., partner with local musicians from various genres and cultures through artists in schools projects).

outcomes.statement: Improvise on an instrument or with voice or other creative technology, exploring and experimenting with music theory, cultural or performance practice.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Improvise around a given structure and in free form.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore how improvisation is used within a variety of genres.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine the work of musicians engaged in improvisation.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate growth in the presentation and construction of improvisation

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Demonstrate knowledge of selected musical concepts (e.g., elements of music, composition principles) through improvisation.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Demonstrate aural skills.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Imitate or transcribe musical ideas (e.g., listen and play).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Develop language appropriate to the musical genre and style to talk about improvisation.

outcomes.statement: Investigate and respond to powwow and other social music of Saskatchewan First Nations peoples.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Engage with First Nations Elders, Knowledge Keepers and/or musicians to introduce music associated with round dance and various powwow dances (e.g., fancy dance, men’s and women’s traditional, jingle dress).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss ways of knowing and learning (e.g., songs passed down/gifted, songs composed) that are applied to learning First Nations traditional and contemporary music.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize how the work of contemporary musicians is influenced by traditional First Nationsmusic.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Examine how music and musicians, including current Saskatchewan musicians, influence and respond to social, political and cultural issues (e.g., treaty education outcome SI10 - examine the spirit and intent of Treaties and investigate [within the context of music] the extent to which they have been fulfilled).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify how First Nations music is used for different purposes (e.g., public songs, social songs, ceremonial songs).

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Describe protocols for singing and drumming at powwows including different gender roles.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explore the differences in music and protocols among First Nations.

outcomes.statement: Investigate and respond to the music of Saskatchewan Métis peoples.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Engage with Métis musicians to introduce characteristics of traditional Métis music.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Discuss ways of knowing and learning (e.g., songs passed down, songs composed) that are applied to learning traditional and contemporary Métis music.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize how the work of contemporary Métis musicians is influenced by traditional music.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Describe various purposes for Métis music (e.g., celebration, storytelling, dance accompaniment, competition).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Examine how Métis music and musicians in Saskatchewan influence and respond to social, political and cultural issues.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Explore the regional and/or stylistic differences in Métis music (e.g., kitchen parties, reels, spoons, crooked tunes, jigging and other dances).

outcomes.statement: Listen and respond critically to own musical expressions and, with guidance, set short term goals for musical growth.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Examine own musical expressions, using teacher feedback and self-assessment, in order to improve.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Respond to qualities of musical elements such as tone, pitch, dynamics and rhythm as well as style, intonation and phrasing within own musical expressions.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: With guidance, generate technique-related inquiry questions and set short term goals for personal improvement based on the inquiry findings.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Apply methods to improve sound quality through care and maintenance of instruments and/or voices.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Identify equipment (e.g., instruments, accessories, amplification systems, acoustical designs, technologies) that impacts sound quality.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into ways technology (e.g., microphones, software, pedals) and materials (e.g., drum heads, mutes, baffles, curtains) can manipulate sound.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Explain relationships between acoustics and sound, experiment with acoustics of various environments and discuss acoustic design considerations.

outcomes.statement: Listen and respond to musical expressions of others, differentiating between critical analysis and personal preference.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Express initial reactions, while listening to music, and conduct further analysis based on evidence in the work.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine and classify music representing various genres, styles, time periods, places, social groups, world cultures, composers and performers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Respond critically (e.g., written, oral, arts expression) to music from various genres, styles, times, places, social groups and cultures using terminology specific to the music genre.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Analyse the characteristics of excellent performance through listening to and watching other performers.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explain relationships between acoustics and sound.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Analyse and interpret music using evidence from the piece and/or performance including examination of the importance of musical text.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Make personal connections to the music and provide reasons for individual preferences.

outcomes.statement: Identify characteristics of the different eras, genres and styles through listening to and/or performing the representative music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify musical, cultural, aural, textual clues that indicate the music’s place and time.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the influence of cultural and historical contexts on the creation of selected music.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the influence of personal experience and place on the creation of selected music.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into how music from the past is recreated today, or how music of today can be reinterpreted in styles from the past.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore the evolution of instruments, voice and creative technologies and their use in various world cultures and time periods.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify protocols for audience and performer according to norms within the genre.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Respond as an audience member and perform in a manner appropriate to the genre (e.g., First Nations powwow, symphony, jazz, African or Latin percussion drum group, rock band) respecting cultural protocols and performance norms (e.g., deportment, attire, respect for local tradition, awaiting invitation to join jam session, bowing, encore).

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Anticipate and prepare for how audiences might react to the music performed in relation to, for example, venue, genre, demographics or type of event.

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Investigate the origins of performance and audience etiquette (e.g., clapping following jazz solos, silence between symphonic movements) in different genres of music.

indicators.label: j
indicators.text: Examine ways in which audience responses in different musical genres affect the musician’s performance and the audience’s experience.

outcomes.statement: Describe the impact and role of music in own life and identify music careers and pathways for continuing engagement in music.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate relationships between music and personal wellness including mental health (e.g., music therapy) and identify and discuss associated research.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Examine ways that different genres/styles of music influence one’s wellbeing (e.g., mood, anxiety, sense of peace) and examine how music is used in media and infused in daily life (e.g., to influence consumers via advertising, shopping environments).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Make connections between music and other areas of study (e.g., literature, math, science, social sciences, physical education, other arts).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Explore opportunities and benefits for continuing lifelong engagement in music (e.g., community choirs, bands, musical theatre).

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into career opportunities in music and investigate opportunities (e.g., career avenues in specific disciplines, scholarships, entrepreneurial skills required, performance contract fees, licensing and financial compensation for digital distribution of recordings) for continuing the study of music.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Examine ways that First Nations musicians learn to sing and play in powwow drum groups.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Examine legalities (e.g., copyrighting, trademarking, First Nations traditional laws, contracts) and ethics (e.g., illegal downloading, sampling, cultural protocols, compensation from streaming services) related to creating and producing music.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Research supports for musicians such as unions, professional associations, agents, Elders and Knowledge Keepers, provincial and federal grants (e.g., funding for creation, touring and recording).

indicators.label: i
indicators.text: Discuss entrepreneurship and personal qualities required for pursuing a career in music.

outcomes.statement: Explore the lives and work of local, Canadian and international musicians.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify, listen to and discuss the work of musicians who have made an impact on music.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate why influential musicians (e.g., current, historical, community) and music educators (e.g., Kodaly, John-Baptiste Arcand, Orff, Buffy Sainte-Marie, Jose Antonio Abreu) and their work are/were influential.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Examine how music and musicians influence and respond to social, political and cultural issues(e.g., representing gender and sexual diversity, concern for environmental sustainability or human rights, world music activists).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Conduct an inquiry into how change (e.g., personal, social, technology) influences musical works.

indicators.label: e

indicators.text: Identify examples of implied or indirect language and examine purpose such as hedging and avoidances after listening, viewing or reading discourse.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify the form of discourse chosen to match the purpose and audience after listening, viewing or reading discourse.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify the dilemma or conflicts and resolution faced by the main character in moral stories.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect on personal lessons learned from moral stories.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Identify examples of puns and jokes and examine their construct and purpose such as gentle criticism or audience involvement.

outcomes.statement: Perform language functions in Nakoda for research.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Consult with community Elders and identify a research need or purpose to gather information on the Nakoda culture.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Formulate research questions.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify possible sources of information including people, written texts and media texts.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Practise and approach cultural resource people with appropriate protocol for collecting information.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Evaluate information critically.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Organize information in ways to fit the need or purpose of task.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Follow protocol for acknowledging sources.

indicators.label: h
indicators.text: Explore effective forms for recording and presenting or using research findings such as incorporating technology, visual presentation, a magazine article or written report.

outcomes.statement: Perform language functions to produce discourse in Nakoda.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Defend a point of view on an issue such as a position taken on learning languages or political involvement

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Retell a traditional moral narrative orally with a focus on developing the main character (e.g., strengths, weaknesses, dilemma, problem, resolution, lesson).

outcomes.statement: Assess personal strengths and needs within the development of language skills and set goals for future improvement.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Reflect on and identifies through the Nakoda worldview and language.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Recognize that speaking, listening and viewing are useful tools to clarify thinking, communicate with others and learn.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Evaluate the quality of own contributions to group process and sets goals and plans for further development.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Develop and use criteria for evaluating self, goals and projects.

outcomes.statement: Assess personal strengths and needs within the development of language learning as they relate to self, family and community and set goals for future improvement.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Assess work for clarity, correctness and impact.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Monitor personal communication goals.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Reflect on attainment of personal goals for effective language learning and use.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Determine personal inquiry and research strengths and language goals.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Reflect on feedback and self-assessment and refine goals.

indicators.label: f
indicators.text: Review new knowledge of Nakoda and its value to self and the wider community.

indicators.label: g
indicators.text: Analyze and assess strategies used while learning Nakoda.

outcomes.statement: Assess personal strengths and needs as a Nakoda speaker and contributions made to the community of learners.

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify what proficient Nakoda speakers do.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Reflect on what one can do on one’s own to learn more as a result of previous learning.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Evaluate who might be approached to learn more about the Nakoda language.

outcomes.statement: Recognize and document the potential of photography as a communication medium through the exploration of a variety of images.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 1: Introduction to Photography (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Describe and compare the aspects of a variety of purposes for photography (e.g., news report, wedding, advertising, hobby, art).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare a snapshot to a photograph with an impact that has endured through time (e.g., World Trade Centre, the Hindenburg Disaster, Terry Fox).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Discuss and categorize different styles of photography (e.g., journalism, portraiture, landscape) given a series of photographs.

outcomes.statement: Identify and demonstrate the controls and functions of a camera.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2A: Camera Controls and Functions (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Demonstrate and explain the proper procedures to:
- hold a camera securely to reduce camera shake
- turn the camera on and of
- manipulate the modes and/or settings on the camera
- preview the image that the camera will take using the viewfinder or display
- focus the lens
- take, review, and delete images
- turn flash on and off (if available)
- connect accessories such as tripod, flash, and cables.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Identify similarities and differences between controls of various cameras including examples of film and digital devices.

outcomes.statement: Capture images that demonstrate advanced camera functions and controls.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 2B: Camera Controls and Functions (Core) · Suggested Time: 5-8 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Select and display tools that can be manipulated (e.g., white balance, histogram, exposure compensation, automatic bracketing).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Select and adjust a variety of camera functions when shooting pictures including:
- metering modes
- focus modes and points
- frame rates
- flash settings (e.g., rear and front curtain sync, manual vs. ttl).

outcomes.statement: Assess and demonstrate the effects of utilizing the photographic triangle (i.e., shutter speed, aperture, and ISO) when capturing an image.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3A: Basic Photographic Skills (Core) · Suggested Time: 15-20 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify the relationships of exposure values on a camera to the amount of light for the exposure.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create images to demonstrate the effects of different shutter speeds, aperture settings, and ISO settings.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Create a wide variety of images by combining techniques and principles of shutter speed, aperture, and ISO.

outcomes.statement: Utilize and extend skills from Module 3A to capture images of increasing quality and refinement.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3B: Basic Photographic Skills (Core) · Suggested Time: 15-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 3A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create a variety of images demonstrating planning, including awareness of aspects such as focus, light manipulation, framing, and the photographic triangle.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a log of camera settings, personal reflections, and knowledge regarding increasing skill level.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Load and unload the storage media from the camera.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate proficiency of image capture through manipulation of camera settings.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 3C: Basic Photographic Skills (Core) · Suggested Time: 15-20 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 3B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Consistently create quality images through control of the exposure triangle.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Consistently create quality images that are in focus, demonstrate basic composition rules, and have a clear focal point.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Create a log of camera settings which includes a personal assessment of each image based on the above criteria.

outcomes.statement: Describe safe and sustainable practices connected to the field of photography.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 4: Safety and Sustainability (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: List safety issues and produce a plan for personal safety when taking photographs.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a list of safety practices to protect both equipment and self when using photographic equipment such as cameras, flash, external lighting.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify environmentally sustainable ways to use and dispose of equipment and accessories such as batteries and chemicals.

outcomes.statement: Create images through demonstration of visualization and composition.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 5: Composition (Core) · Suggested Time: 8-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 3A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research and define elements of photographic critique.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Critique various photos on their compositional merit.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Visualize and describe or illustrate techniques to compose a photograph.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create images demonstrating aspects of composition such as rule of thirds, negative space, lines, contrast, and colour.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Recognize when normal rules of compostion can be broken.

outcomes.statement: Analyze the effect of focal length on the image.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6A: Focal Length and Camera Lenses (Core) · Suggested Time: 6-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 2A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Show the effects on a series of images produced by changing the focal length (i.e., zoom).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a series of images to demonstrate how perspective is changed by altering the camera position relative to the subject.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Produce a series of images to show the apparent change in depth of field resulting from a change in focal length.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate an understanding of selecting various lenses and focal lengths to create a variety of effects on the image.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 6B: Focal Length and Camera Lenses (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 6A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Illustrate how different lenses affect an image (e.g., fast versus slow, zoom versus prime).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate the change in image as a result of using a variety of lenses (e.g., fisheye, wide angle, telephoto).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Understand and illustrate, through providing examples, the concept of how a resulting image is affected by focal length and/or format size.

outcomes.statement: Create a series of images showing the effect of the quality, quantity, and direction of light.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 7: Understanding Light (Core) · Suggested Time: 7-8 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 3A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text:
Explore and demonstrate the effect of changing:
- the direction of light on a subject
- the quality of light on a subject including diffuse light, natural light, colour, temperature, and types of light sources
- the quantity of light on a subject.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Manipulate light to change the resulting image through the use of tools such as reflectors, diffusers, coloured gels, and additional light sources.

outcomes.statement: Explore and evaluate the career training and occupational opportunities in the field of photography in Saskatchewan, Canada, and globally, including post-secondary education programs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 8: Career and Occupational Opportunities (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify specific examples of occupational skills required in photography occupations.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate programs offered by universities and technical institutes in photography.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the career opportunities for professional photographers.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Identify local opportunities for being paid as a freelance photographer.

outcomes.statement: Create images demonstrating the use of an electronic flash.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 9: Electronic Flash (Optional) · Suggested Time: 5-7 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 7

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Compare images that demonstrate the effects of using an electronic flash.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Demonstrate the effects of changing the flash technique (e.g., bounce, using diffusers, or using coloured gels on the flash).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Show the effects of manipulating flash through power settings (e.g., full power, half power).

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate the use of mixed lighting and fill-in flash.

outcomes.statement: Optimize colour values when capturing an image.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 10: Colour Balance/White Balance (Core) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 7

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate how changes in white balance can be manipulated to produce different effects.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Adjust the colour balance on a camera to achieve different visual impacts in different lighting situations to represent what you see.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate how to set a custom white balance for specific locations, light sources, and conditions.

outcomes.statement: Develop a workflow to improve digital images using software.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11A: Image Adjustment (Core) · Suggested Time: 8-10 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 5

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Crop images to create a better composition.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Resize images for various outputs.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Demonstrate and explain why and how files are saved in different formats.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Demonstrate and explain how and why files are saved with different resolutions.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Adjust brightness, colour, and contrast to enhance a photograph.

outcomes.statement: Continue to develop proficiency with software to improve digital images.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11B: Image Adjustment (Core) · Suggested Time: 8-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 11A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Use curves to adjust brightness, contrast, and colour saturation and tone.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Apply various types of filters when adjusting an image (e.g., sharpening, texturizing, blur, black and white).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Use software tools to retouch an image.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate increasing expertise using software to improve digital images.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 11C: Image Adjustment (Core) · Suggested Time: 8-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 11B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Manipulate original images to enhance their appearance.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text:
Apply advanced editing effects to create images such as:
- selection tools
- masking
- brushes
- vignetting
- dodging and burning
- temperature adjustment.

outcomes.statement: Investigate and articulate legal issues related to photography such as copyright and consent.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12A: Legal and Ethical Issues (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: None

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Explain the term “copyright” as used in the Canadian legal system and assess its impact on a photography class.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Investigate the three factors that place some works in the public domain and cite some examples of these works along with reasons for their inclusion.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate and report on current issues and resources connected to copyright law such as “open source”, “creative commons”, and stock resources.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate and report on the need for consent in various circumstances such as location, appearance, and material.

outcomes.statement: Discuss and reflect on the need for societal standards (e.g., legal, ethical, and community norms, and values) and cultural sensitivity in photography.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12B: Legal and Ethical Issues (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 12A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Formulate a list of societal standards in relation to issues such as sexism, racism, and homophobia, and support the list with positive media examples.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compose a strategy for inclusion of appropriate content and images reflective of societal standards in personal, class, and school projects and assignments.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Identify and discuss issues regarding posting of images on the web including safety, possible consequences, and permanence of web postings.

outcomes.statement: Identify through research the positive and negative aspects of creative, artistic, and intellectual works receiving ownership protection.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 12C: Legal and Ethical Issues (Core) · Suggested Time: 2-3 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 12B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Utilize the Canadian Intellectual Property Office to distinguish between copyright, a patent, and an industrial design, and identify some common examples pertaining to photography.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Collect and categorize a number of articles from various sources regarding intellectual property that reflect opposing points of view.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Explain and support a personal stance on intellectual property.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Investigate the ownership rights of personal work and how to protect and sell usage rights of personal work using techniques such as watermarking.

outcomes.statement: Develop skills using basic image editing software to manipulate photographs.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13A: Image Manipulation (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 11A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate a variety of manipulation techniques such as compositing, distorting, and perspective control.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compare original and manipulated images to examine the different messages of each.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Recognize and discuss some of the ethical implications in image manipulations.

outcomes.statement: Continue to develop skills using basic image editing software to manipulate photographs for a defined purpose.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13B: Image Manipulation (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 13A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Demonstrate techniques such as retouching, skin correction, contrast, layering, panoramas, stitching, and masking as examples of manipulation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Provide personal and ethical justification for choosing manipulation procedures to enhance an image.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate increasing expertise using software to perform advanced manipulation of digital images.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 13C: Image Manipulation (Core) · Suggested Time: 10-15 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 13B

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Apply software/editing effects to create personally satisfying images.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Manipulate an image to alter the appearance (e.g., colour, apparent age, masking).

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Restore old or damaged photographs.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Apply tone-mapping using multiple images.

indicators.label: e
indicators.text: Explore high dynamic range (HDR) photography.

outcomes.statement: Develop abilities to critique photographic work as a means of evaluation and self-reflection of personal, peer, and public work.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 14: Critiquing Images (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 5

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Research and discuss various aspects of critiquing work (aesthetic and technical merits).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a critique of acquired images produced by self and peers.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Express an opinion based on knowledge of composition, genre, design, style, message, presentation, and target audience.

outcomes.statement: Explore and demonstrate a variety of presentation formats that photographers use to display work.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15A: Presentations/Sharing of Images (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 14

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Maintain a personal portfolio reflecting growth in understanding and skills involved in image creation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Compile personal images for display.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Select a style and venue for a school or public showing.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Practise aspects of presentations such as matting, mounting, and framing.

outcomes.statement: Create and display a digital or print gallery of completed images along with photographer’s notes and descriptions of the process involved.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 15B: Presentations/Sharing of Images (Optional) · Suggested Time: 10-20 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 15A

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Create a plan for an exhibition including time, space, intended audience, and purpose.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a personally satisfying photography presentation through the use of matting, mounting, and/or framing.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Engage classmates and/or the public in a display of personally created photographs.

indicators.label: d
indicators.text: Create an assessment of the exhibition through personal reflection and feedback from others.

outcomes.statement: Demonstrate skills and processes used by photojournalists.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 16: Photojournalism (Optional) · Suggested Time: 6-8 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 8

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate and report on what a photojournalist does.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Choose a theme and document an event through the use of images and captions in the style of a photojournalist.

outcomes.statement: Develop skills and processes used in commercial photography to promote a product or service.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 17: Advertising and Product Photography (Optional) · Suggested Time: 8-10 hours · Level: Intermediate · Prerequisite: Module 8

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Critique an existing advertisement on the effectiveness of the photography.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a series of images of various products.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Create a fictional draft advertisement using an existing campaign or a personal example.

outcomes.statement: Develop and demonstrate techniques employed by portrait photographers.
outcomes.printedWith: Develop and demonstrate techniques employed by portrait photographers. (Optional) · Suggested Time: 8-10 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 7

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate the effects of lighting on subjects (e.g., supplementary lighting, reflectors).

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Explore how various poses create emphasis.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Practise group arrangements to produce an effective group portrait.

outcomes.statement: Develop required skills to operate a variety of photographic businesses.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 19: Entrepreneurship (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Advanced · Prerequisite: Module 8

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Identify and interview an entrepreneur to investigate how he/she started out in business and what advice he/she can provide.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Analyze the differences between photojournalism, social photography (e.g., weddings, parties), portrait photography, assignment photography and stock photography and create a statement about your personal business preference.

indicators.label: c
indicators.text: Investigate the costs of starting a photography business such as buying equipment, obtaining a business licence, paying taxes, pricing your product, and purchasing insurance.

outcomes.statement: Explore and articulate the major historical developments in photography.
outcomes.printedWith: Module 20: History of Photography (Optional) · Suggested Time: 3-5 hours · Level: Introductory · Prerequisite: Module 1

indicators.label: a
indicators.text: Investigate a photographic process (e.g., camera obscura, daguerreotype, tintype) and share the knowledge through a photographic presentation.

indicators.label: b
indicators.text: Create a visual presentation to present the work of a single noted phototgrapher or to compare the styles of two or more photographers including how they contributed to advancements in the art or science of the field.
